title.zh: 职场婚恋小说怎么写：让事业与感情互相改变选择
title.en: Writing Workplace Romance: Let Work and Love Change Each Other

seo_title.zh: 职场婚恋小说怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Workplace Romance | ZenStory

description.zh: 把项目目标、专业判断、公开评价和亲密边界放进同一事件，让两条线互为代价。
description.en: Put project goals, professional judgment, public appraisal and relationship boundaries into one event, so gains in one storyline cost the other.

answer.zh: 职场婚恋要让事业线和关系线在同一选择上互相施压。人物各自有专业目标、组织责任和亲密需求；工作结果改变信任与公开边界，关系选择也带来项目、职位、客户或团队后果。行业细节只保留会改变判断与行动的部分。
answer.en: In workplace romance, career and relationship pressures should meet in the same choice. Each character has professional goals, organisational responsibilities and personal needs. Work outcomes change trust and the boundaries of what is public; relationship choices affect projects, positions, clients or teams. Keep only industry details that change judgments and actions.

heading.zh: 先把题材发动机写清
heading.en: Define the Story Engine

body.zh: 每个主要单元写两句话：工作上谁要交付什么，关系上谁希望对方怎样表态。然后找一件无法分别处理的事件，让同一个决定同时影响两条线。办公室流言只是压力载体，真正冲突落在署名、回避、资源分配、客户承诺或是否公开关系。
body.en: For each major story unit, write two sentences: who must deliver what at work, and who wants the other person to take what stance in the relationship. Then find an event that cannot be handled separately, so one decision affects both storylines. Office gossip is only a means of exerting pressure. The real conflict concerns credit, stepping aside from decisions, resource allocation, commitments to clients or whether to make the relationship public.

heading.zh: 怎样持续推进而不重复
heading.en: Keep Progressing Without Repetition

body.zh:
| 单元检查 | 例子 |
|---|---|
| 专业分歧 | 一个方案保客户，一个方案保护团队 |
| 权力边界 | 上下级能否共同评审与回避表决 |
| 公开代价 | 承认关系会影响谁的信誉与机会 |
| 私人需求 | 支持对方是否意味着放弃自己的目标 |

感情推进通过共同解决、拒绝代替、承认错误和重新分权完成。亲密动作不能替代职业后果。
body.en:
| What to check in a story unit | Example |
|---|---|
| Professional disagreement | One proposal protects the client; another protects the team |
| Limits of authority | Whether a manager and subordinate can review together and abstain from voting |
| Cost of disclosure | Whose reputation or opportunities will be affected by acknowledging the relationship |
| Personal needs | Whether supporting the other person means giving up one’s own goal |

Develop the relationship through solving problems together, refusing to decide for the other person, admitting mistakes and redistributing authority. Intimate gestures cannot replace professional consequences.

heading.zh: 原创范例
heading.en: Original Example

body.zh:
城市展览公司里，项目经理叶知与灯光师周昱隐瞒恋爱关系。客户要求删掉安全测试以赶期开幕，周昱拒绝签字；叶知若支持他，会失去刚获得的项目主导权。她没有私下让他退让，而是在项目会议上向主管及验收组说明两人的恋爱关系，提交延期方案，并主动申请退出灯光验收表决。

项目延期，团队保住测试；恋爱关系进入主管及验收组的知情范围，却建立了可执行的回避规则。下一阶段冲突来自职位竞争，而非重复猜忌。
body.en:
At a city exhibition company, project manager Ye Zhi and lighting specialist Zhou Yu are keeping their romantic relationship secret. The client wants to drop safety testing to open on schedule, but Zhou Yu refuses to sign off. Supporting him would cost Ye Zhi her newly acquired control of the project. Instead of privately asking him to give in, she tells the supervisor and acceptance-review group about their relationship at a project meeting. She submits a postponement proposal and asks to withdraw from the lighting-acceptance vote.

The project is delayed and the team keeps the tests. The supervisor and review group now know about the relationship, but an enforceable rule for stepping aside from decisions has been established. The next phase’s conflict comes from competition for a position rather than repeated suspicion.

heading.zh: 常见写偏与修正
heading.en: Common Missteps and Fixes

body.zh:
| 写偏 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 职场只是约会背景 | 给每场工作明确交付和责任 |
| 行业术语像汇报 | 只写会改变选择的流程与证据 |
| 爱情自动解决事业困难 | 让双方保留专业分歧和独立代价 |
| 靠反复误会拉扯 | 用公开边界、共同决策和后果推进 |

复查每次关系推进时，追踪它对工作分工、公开评价或退出选择造成的后果；再检查项目结果是否反过来改变信任。两条线连续数章互不影响，说明其中一条只是装饰，需要在下一次决定中重新相交。
body.en:
| Misstep | Fix |
|---|---|
| The workplace is only a backdrop for dates | Give each work scene a clear deliverable and responsibility |
| Industry terminology sounds like a report | Include only processes and evidence that change choices |
| Love automatically solves career problems | Let both people retain professional disagreements and costs of their own |
| Repeated misunderstandings provide all the tension | Progress through disclosure boundaries, joint decisions and consequences |

For every advance in the relationship, track its effects on the division of work, public appraisal or the option to walk away. Then check whether the project’s outcome changes trust in return. If the two storylines have no effect on each other for several chapters, one is merely decorative. Bring them together again in the next decision.

q.zh: 这种方法需要固定章节数吗？
q.en: Does this method require a fixed number of chapters?

a.zh: 不需要。章节与阶段由故事实际变化决定，表格只帮助检查因果、资源与关系是否前进。
a.en: No. Chapters and phases follow the story’s actual changes. The table only helps check whether cause and effect, resources and relationships are moving forward.

q.zh: 可以直接套用示例情节吗？
q.en: Can I reuse the example plot directly?

a.zh: 示例用于展示方法。应替换故事发动机、人物选择与后果，避免只改姓名和场景。
a.en: The example demonstrates the method. Replace the story engine, character choices and consequences rather than merely changing names and locations.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 按本文方法规划我的故事，先写核心承诺、人物目标和可持续推进方式，不写完整正文”（Codex 里使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /story-long-write to plan my story with this article’s method. Start with the core promise, character goals and a sustainable way to move the story forward. Do not write the full prose.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说人物设定集怎么整理：角色、时间线与知识边界模板
title.en: Organising a Story Bible: Characters, Timelines and Knowledge

seo_title.zh: 小说人物设定集怎么整理｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Organise a Story Bible | ZenStory

description.zh: 把静态人设、当前状态、关系、时间线、世界规则和未结事项分开维护，减少长篇设定冲突。
description.en: Maintain stable character facts, current states, relationships, timelines, world rules and open threads separately to reduce continuity conflicts.

answer.zh: 长篇设定集要区分稳定事实和会随剧情变化的状态。角色卡保存身份、底线与长期目标；当前状态只记录位置、资源、关系、已知信息和未结事项的最新值；时间线保存客观顺序，知识边界另记角色与读者各自知道什么。发生变化时更新对应位置，避免多份真相并存。
answer.en: A long-form story bible should distinguish stable facts from states that change with the plot. Character profiles hold identity, boundaries and long-term goals. Current-state records keep only the latest location, resources, relationships, known information and unresolved matters. A timeline records the objective sequence, while separate knowledge records track what characters and readers each know. Update the appropriate place when something changes so conflicting versions of the truth do not accumulate.

heading.zh: 一套够用的设定集
heading.en: A Story Bible That Covers the Essentials

body.zh:
| 模块 | 保存内容 | 更新时机 |
|---|---|---|
| 角色卡 | 身份、经历、能力边界、长期目标 | 设定被正式改变 |
| 当前状态 | 位置、资源、关系、已知、未结事项 | 每次发生有效变化 |
| 关系表 | 双方承诺、债务、公开与私下位置 | 关系动作落地 |
| 作者时间线 | 客观事件顺序与日期 | 新事实确认 |
| 读者已知 | 正文已经揭示的内容 | 章节完成 |
| 世界规则 | 适用条件、例外、代价 | 规则建立或修订 |

同一事实指定一个权威位置，其余文件只引用或记录当前结果。
body.en:
| Module | What it stores | When to update it |
|---|---|---|
| Character profile | Identity, history, ability limits and long-term goals | When an established fact is formally changed |
| Current state | Location, resources, relationships, knowledge and open matters | After each meaningful change |
| Relationship record | Mutual promises, debts and how the relationship stands in public and in private | When an action changes the relationship |
| Author’s timeline | Objective event order and dates | When a new fact is confirmed |
| Reader knowledge | What the prose has already revealed | When a chapter is finished |
| World rules | Conditions, exceptions and costs | When a rule is established or revised |

Give each fact one authoritative home. Other files should refer to it or record only the resulting current state.

heading.zh: 可复制的角色状态模板
heading.en: A Character-State Template to Copy

body.zh:
> **截至章节**：
> **当前位置与正在执行的行动**：
> **当前目标**：
> **能力与可用资源**：
> **关键关系**：对每个重要对象写承诺、债务和边界
> **本人已知／误信／隐瞒**：
> **未结事项**：
> **本次变化来源**：

只为后续会复用的角色建状态页。一次性路人留在章节记录，避免设定集膨胀。修订旧章时，从改动点向后重算受影响的状态。
body.en:
> **Current as of chapter:**
> **Present location and action underway:**
> **Current goal:**
> **Abilities and available resources:**
> **Key relationships:** Record promises, debts and boundaries for each important person.
> **What the character knows / falsely believes / conceals:**
> **Unresolved matters:**
> **Source of this change:**

Create state pages only for characters who will recur. Leave one-off passers-by in chapter notes to keep the story bible manageable. When revising an earlier chapter, work forward from the change and recalculate the affected states.

heading.zh: 原创填写示例：旧水站管理员
heading.en: Original Filled-In Example: The Old Water Station’s Caretaker

body.zh:
> **截至章节**：第十二章
> **当前位置与行动**：旧水站值班室，准备关闭北线阀门
> **当前目标**：在检修队到达前证明污染来自回流管
> **资源**：值班钥匙、过去三日压力表；没有取样权限
> **关键关系**：欠居民代表一次公开说明；与站长的口头保密约定已破裂
> **已知**：北线夜间压力异常；**误信**：检修队已收到完整记录
> **未结事项**：谁删掉了凌晨数据；钥匙为何被复制

这份当前状态省去童年和外貌，专门保存下一章会约束行动的事实。
body.en:
> **Current as of chapter:** Chapter twelve
> **Location and action:** The old water station’s duty room, preparing to close the northern-line valve
> **Current goal:** Prove that contamination comes from the return pipe before the maintenance crew arrives
> **Resources:** Duty keys and pressure records from the past three days; no authority to take samples
> **Key relationships:** Owes the residents’ representative a public explanation; the verbal confidentiality agreement with the station manager has broken down
> **Knows:** Northern-line pressure is abnormal at night; **falsely believes:** the maintenance crew has received the complete records
> **Unresolved matters:** Who deleted the early-morning data, and why the key was copied

This current-state record omits childhood and appearance. It stores the facts that will constrain action in the next chapter.

heading.zh: 发现冲突时怎样分级
heading.en: Prioritise Conflicts When You Find Them

body.zh: 先找明文事实，再核规则条件、时间顺序、因果和代价。直接互斥或破坏主线的冲突优先处理；隐性因果断裂其次；外貌小差异单独记录；伏笔超期属于提醒。每条问题都引用前提、触发事件和矛盾点。设定集负责给证据，不替作者判断哪条剧情更好。
body.en: Locate explicit facts first, then check rule conditions, chronological order, cause and effect, and costs. Address direct contradictions or conflicts that break the main storyline first, followed by less obvious causal gaps. Record minor appearance discrepancies separately; overdue foreshadowing belongs among reminders. For each issue, cite the premise, the triggering event and the point of contradiction. The story bible supplies evidence. It does not decide for the author which plot is better.

q.zh: 这种方法需要固定章节数吗？
q.en: Does this method require a fixed number of chapters?

a.zh: 不需要。章节与阶段由故事实际变化决定，表格只帮助检查因果、资源与关系是否前进。
a.en: No. Let actual changes in the story determine chapters and stages. The table only helps check whether causality, resources, and relationships are moving forward.

q.zh: 可以直接套用示例情节吗？
q.en: Can I reuse the example plot directly?

a.zh: 示例用于展示方法。应替换故事发动机、人物选择与后果，避免只改姓名和场景。
a.en: The example demonstrates the method. Replace the story engine, character choices, and consequences rather than merely changing names and locations.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /story-long-write（Codex 中用 $story-long-write）根据我提供的设定与已写正文整理或更新设定集：分开稳定事实、当前状态、客观时间线、角色已知与误信、刻意隐瞒和未结事项。只使用实际读到的材料；冲突和缺失先列为待确认项，不替我编造前史。本轮不写章节正文。
text.en: In Claude Code, use /story-long-write (in Codex, use $story-long-write) to organise or update a story bible from the setting notes and prose I provide. Separate stable facts, current states, the objective timeline, what characters know and falsely believe, deliberate concealment and unresolved matters. Use only material actually read. List conflicts and gaps for confirmation rather than inventing a backstory for me. Do not write chapter prose in this round.

title.zh: 小说封面提示词怎么写：题材、构图和文字分层
title.en: Writing Novel-Cover Prompts: Separate Genre, Composition and Text

seo_title.zh: 小说封面提示词怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Writing Novel-Cover Prompts | ZenStory

description.zh: 从题材承诺提炼主体、背景、色彩和光线，再把书名与作者名作为独立文字层处理。
description.en: Translate a genre promise into subject, background, colour and light. Treat the title and author name as separate text layers.

answer.zh: 小说封面提示词先提炼一个最重要的阅读承诺，再选择能让人一眼识别题材的主体、场景与色彩。提示词按主体、动作或关系、前中远景、光线、版式和文字预留区分层描述。书名与作者名独立处理，并在生成后人工核对文字、辨识度和使用权限。
answer.en: Start a novel-cover prompt with the reading promise that matters most, then choose a subject, setting and palette that make the genre recognisable at a glance. Describe the subject, action or relationship, foreground/midground/background, lighting, layout and reserved text areas in separate layers. Handle the title and author name separately. After generation, manually check the lettering, legibility and usage rights.

heading.zh: 先把题材翻译成视觉证据
heading.en: Turn the Genre into Visual Evidence

body.zh:
| 题材承诺 | 主体证据 | 背景证据 | 色彩与光线 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 玄幻成长 | 人物、法器、资格徽记 | 山门、试炼场、远层势力 | 深色环境配一处能量焦点 |
| 都市脑洞 | 普通人和异常物件 | 办公室、街道、账单或屏幕 | 现实冷色配异常亮色 |
| 悬疑追查 | 证物、背影、受限空间 | 雨夜、档案室、空房 | 高反差与局部照明 |
| 情感关系 | 两人的距离和视线 | 共享空间或分隔物 | 与关系温度一致 |

题材元素只保留最能证明承诺的一两项，避免把所有梗都塞上封面。
body.en:
| Genre promise | Evidence in the subject | Evidence in the background | Colour and lighting |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fantasy progression | A character, magical artefact or mark of rank | A mountain gate, trial grounds or distant faction | Dark surroundings with one point of energy |
| Urban speculative fiction | An ordinary person and an anomalous object | An office, street, bill, or screen | Cool realistic colours with one anomalous bright accent |
| Mystery investigation | Evidence, a figure seen from behind or a confined space | A rainy night, archive room or empty house | High contrast and localised lighting |
| Emotional relationship | The distance and eyelines between two people | A shared space or something separating them | Lighting and colour temperature suited to the relationship |

Keep only the one or two elements that best prove the genre promise. Do not crowd the cover with every story idea.

heading.zh: 可复用的提示词结构
heading.en: A Reusable Prompt Structure

body.zh:
> 竖版小说封面；核心阅读承诺；主要人物或象征物及其动作；前景／中景／远景层次；主色与点缀色；光源方向和情绪；顶部保留清晰书名区，底部保留作者名区；整体插画或海报质感；排除水印与无关文字。

文字内容、字体风格、位置与颜色单列。任何生成工具对文字的表现都需要成图后核对；必要时先生成无字底图，再在排版软件中添加准确文字。页面不承诺具体模型一定正确输出中文。
body.en:
> Vertical novel cover; core reading promise; main character or symbolic object and its action; foreground / midground / background; main and accent colours; light direction and mood; clear title area at the top and author-name area at the bottom; illustrated-poster finish; no watermark or unrelated text.

List the wording, font style, placement and colour separately. Check any text produced by an image tool against the finished image; if necessary, generate a text-free background first and add accurate lettering in layout software. This page does not promise that a particular model will render Chinese text correctly.

heading.zh: 原创范例：《雾港回声簿》
heading.en: Original Example: The Ledger of Fog Harbor

body.zh:
这是一本都市悬疑：档案员能听见被涂改记录留下的声音。提示词可写：

> 竖版悬疑小说封面，一名年轻档案员侧身站在狭长档案库中央，手中摊开的登记簿浮出细弱声波纹；前景是被红笔覆盖的姓名栏，中景是人物与台灯，远景的金属档案架消失在雾中；墨蓝和灰白为主色，只用暗红标记涂改处；单一冷光从上方照亮书页；顶部留出大面积干净标题区，底部留作者名区；克制的插画海报感，无水印、无额外文字。

书名和署名应在单独排版阶段按真实内容添加。
body.en:
This is an urban mystery about an archivist who can hear the sounds left behind in altered records. A prompt might read:

> Vertical mystery-novel cover. A young archivist stands in profile in the centre of a narrow records archive. Faint sound waves rise from an open ledger in their hands. In the foreground, a name field is crossed out in red ink; in the midground are the archivist and a desk lamp; in the background, metal filing shelves fade into mist. Ink blue and grey-white dominate, with dark red only to mark the altered entry. A single cool light from above illuminates the page. Leave a large, clean title area at the top and an author-name area at the bottom. Restrained illustrated-poster style. No watermark or extra text.

Add the actual title and byline during a separate layout step.

heading.zh: 生成或设计后检查什么
heading.en: What to Check After Generating or Designing

body.zh:
缩小到手机缩略图，检查主体与题材是否仍可识别；确认标题区域没有复杂高光和人物面部；核对人物数量、持物、时代服装和故事设定；确认画面没有多余字样、水印或错误符号；检查作者拥有输入素材和最终用途所需的权利。

构图失败时先减少元素、扩大主体或清理文字区。风格词堆得再多，也不能补救阅读承诺不清和信息层级混乱。
body.en:
Reduce the cover to a phone-sized thumbnail and check that the subject and genre are still recognisable. Make sure complex highlights and faces do not intrude on the title area. Check the number of characters, what they are holding, period clothing and consistency with the story. Look for stray lettering, watermarks or incorrect symbols. Confirm you have the rights needed for the input materials and the final use.

If the composition does not work, first remove elements, enlarge the subject or clear the text area. More style keywords will not fix an unclear reading promise or a confused information hierarchy.

q.zh: 书名和作者名应该一起生成，还是后期添加？
q.en: Should the title and author name be generated together or added later?

a.zh: 希望画面与字体统一时，可以在生成请求中明确给出准确文字；需要反复改书名、字体或版式时，可以先做无字底图，再单独排版。两种方式都要逐字核对成图，并检查缩略图下的可读性。
a.en: If you want the image and lettering to feel unified, specify the exact text in the generation prompt. If you expect to revise the title, font or layout, generate a text-free background first and add the type separately. Either way, check every character in the finished image and make sure it remains legible as a thumbnail.

q.zh: 封面元素太多，看不出重点怎么办？
q.en: What should I do if the cover has too many elements and no clear focus?

a.zh: 先留一个能代表故事承诺的主体，删除重复表达题材的装饰物。把标题区从人物脸部、复杂纹理与高光中让出来，再缩小检查主体和书名能否分别读清。
a.en: Keep one subject that represents the story’s promise and remove decorative elements that repeat the genre cues. Clear the title area of faces, complex textures and highlights, then reduce the image to check that both the subject and title remain easy to read.

text.zh: 需要实际生成封面时，在 Claude Code 中用 /story-cover（Codex 中用 $story-cover），提供准确书名、作者名、目标平台和保存目录，并附上题材简介及构图偏好。这个技能会调用图像生成工具并保存封面，不只是输出文字方案。使用你有权提供的参考素材，生成后逐字核对书名、署名和画面内容。
text.en: When you need an actual generated cover, use /story-cover in Claude Code (or $story-cover in Codex). Provide the exact title, author name, target platform and save directory, along with a genre summary and composition preferences. This skill calls an image-generation tool and saves a cover; it does not merely return a text proposal. Use reference materials you have the right to provide, then check the title, byline and image content character by character.

title.zh: 女频小说安全感怎么写：虐有回报，选择有去处
title.en: Women-Focused Web Fiction: Pain, Payoff and Character Choice

seo_title.zh: 女频小说安全感怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Emotional Safety in Women-Focused Web Fiction | ZenStory

description.zh: 用承诺锚点、阶段回报和人物选择维持女频长篇安全感，避免整卷受虐与事后强行补偿。
description.en: Use promise anchors, phase payoffs and character choices to sustain emotional safety. Avoid a whole volume of suffering followed by contrived compensation.

answer.zh: 女频长篇的安全感来自可追踪的承诺：主角会靠自己的选择改变处境，伤害会留下后果，阶段结束会得到成长、边界或关系回报。虐点可以存在，但每段压力都要让人物采取行动，并在继续加压前交付可见进展。
answer.en: Emotional safety in long-form women’s fiction comes from promises readers can track: the protagonist changes her circumstances through her own choices, harm has consequences, and each phase brings a payoff in growth, boundaries or relationships. Painful moments can be part of the story, but each stretch of pressure should lead to character action and visible progress before the pressure increases again.

heading.zh: 先建立三种安全感锚点
heading.en: Establish Three Anchors of Emotional Safety

body.zh:
- **方向锚点**：开篇让读者看见主角准备离开、反击、争取或重建什么。
- **选择锚点**：关键转向由主角作出，帮助和宠爱也要经过她的接受、拒绝或交换。
- **回报锚点**：每个阶段留下可见结果，如收入、住处、话语权、退出能力或新的关系边界。

安全感不等于提前宣布圆满结局。它让读者知道痛苦正在改变人物的行动，而非无限重复。
body.en:
- **Direction anchor:** At the opening, show what the protagonist is preparing to leave, fight back against, pursue or rebuild.
- **Choice anchor:** Let the protagonist make the key turns. Help and affection should still leave room for her acceptance, refusal or negotiation.
- **Payoff anchor:** Give each phase a visible result, such as income, housing, influence, the ability to walk away or a new boundary in a relationship.

Emotional safety does not mean announcing a happy ending in advance. It lets readers see that suffering is changing what the character does rather than repeating endlessly.

heading.zh: 虐点怎样写出剂量与回报
heading.en: Balance Pain with a Payoff

body.zh:
给每段伤害写四行：谁利用什么关系或资源造成伤害；主角当下失去什么；她因此采取哪项新行动；本阶段归还什么控制权或认知。连续压力可以逐步升级，但不能连续整段只增加受害细节。

回报也不限于“被更爱”。主角获得收入、法律或组织支持、可靠盟友、公开署名、拒绝权和离开能力，都能证明局面已动。下一次压力应挑战新边界，避免把刚取得的成长重置。
body.en:
For each stretch of harm, write four lines: who uses which relationship or resource to cause it; what the protagonist loses immediately; what new action she takes as a result; and what control or understanding is restored in this phase. Pressure can escalate, but do not spend a long stretch only adding details of the character’s victimisation.

Payoff does not have to mean “being loved more.” Income, support from a legal or organisational body, a reliable ally, public credit, the right to refuse and the ability to leave can all demonstrate a changed situation. The next pressure should test the new boundary, not reset the growth the character has just achieved.

heading.zh: 原创范例：旧剧院的灯光席
heading.en: Original Example: The Lighting Booth in an Old Theatre

body.zh:
舞台监督许言长期替导演伴侣承担事故责任。一次灯架故障后，对方要求她再次签下“个人操作失误”。许言没有等新角色来救，她先封存当天排练单，暂停自己掌控的灯光席，并通知演员改用工作灯彩排。

她因此失去演出奖金，却迫使剧院召开安全复核。复核只证明设备维护缺失，没有自动修复感情。阶段回报是她获得独立签字权，并搬出共同住处；关系线随后要面对对方是否承认长期转嫁责任。

虐点推动了职业和亲密边界，安全感来自她已经拥有新的行动路径。
body.en:
Stage manager Xu Yan has long taken the blame for accidents on behalf of her partner, a director. After a lighting rig malfunctions, he asks her to sign another statement saying it was “operator error.” Xu Yan does not wait for a new character to rescue her. She first preserves that day’s rehearsal records, shuts down the lighting console she controls and tells the actors to rehearse using work lights instead.

She loses her performance bonus, but forces the theatre to hold a safety review. The review proves only that equipment maintenance was lacking; it does not automatically repair the relationship. The phase payoff is that she gains independent signing authority and moves out of their shared home. The relationship arc must now confront whether her partner will acknowledge having shifted responsibility to her over time.

The painful event advances both professional and personal boundaries. Emotional safety comes from her having a new path of action.

heading.zh: 主情绪怎样保持一致
heading.en: Keep the Central Emotion Consistent

body.zh:
先用一句话写全书主情绪的方向，例如“从总替别人收拾后果，到相信自己的选择值得被尊重”。事业、亲情和爱情可以提供不同场面，但都应推动或挑战这条方向。

复查时问：本单元让主角更能选择，还是又回到只能等待？伤害后的回报是否与伤害对应？简介承诺的翻盘方向是否仍在推进？这些问题比给女频贴固定题材或读者标签更能约束创作。
body.en:
Write the direction of the story’s central emotion in one sentence, such as: “From always cleaning up other people’s messes to believing her own choices deserve respect.” Work, family and romance can provide different scenes, but each should advance or challenge that direction.

During review, ask: Can the protagonist make more choices in this unit, or has she returned to waiting helplessly? Does the payoff after harm correspond to what was lost? Is the turnaround promised in the synopsis still advancing? These questions constrain the writing better than assigning women’s fiction a fixed genre or reader label.

q.zh: 需要按固定阶段或章节数写吗？
q.en: Do I need to use fixed phases or a fixed number of chapters?

a.zh: 不需要。阶段由人物取得的资源、权力、关系与选择发生了什么变化来划分。
a.en: No. Divide phases according to changes in the character’s resources, power, relationships and choices.

q.zh: 示例可以直接换名字使用吗？
q.en: Can I use the example by changing only the names?

a.zh: 示例用于说明方法。新故事应重新设计冲突发动机、人物选择、代价和兑现方式。
a.en: The example illustrates the method. A new story needs its own conflict engine, character choices, costs and payoffs.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 按本文方法规划我的内容，先给可执行方案和原创示例，不虚构平台、模型或效果数据”（Codex 里使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /story-long-write to plan my material with this article’s method. Start with an actionable plan and an original example. Do not invent platform, model or performance data.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 都市脑洞文怎么写：让一个新规则撑起整本书
title.en: Writing Urban Speculative Fiction: Build a Novel Around One New Rule

seo_title.zh: 都市脑洞文怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Urban Speculative Fiction | ZenStory

description.zh: 把脑洞规则放进账单、合同、工作与关系等现实场面，并拆成不重复的收益、风险和公开反馈。
description.en: Put one speculative rule into bills, contracts, work and relationships. Develop distinct gains, risks and public responses instead of repeating rewards.

answer.zh: 都市脑洞先从具体的现实窘境进入，让一条新规则立刻改变人物的选择。规则必须有触发条件、限制和可见结果；长篇能否成立，看它能否持续产生性质不同的现实问题，而非反复发奖励。
answer.en: Open urban speculative fiction with a concrete real-world predicament, then introduce one new rule that immediately changes what a character chooses to do. Give the rule trigger conditions, limits and visible results. To sustain a novel, it must keep producing different kinds of real-world problems rather than repeatedly handing out rewards.

heading.zh: 先写一条可运行的新规则
heading.en: Write One New Rule That Can Operate

body.zh: 用五问定义脑洞：什么条件触发；主角能获得什么；限制或代价是什么；旁人能看见哪种结果；规则被公开、误解或利用后会发生什么。第一次展示只解决一个小问题，让读者从结果理解规则。面板如需出现，只保留当前目标、限制和结果。
body.en: Define the speculative premise by answering five questions: What triggers it? What can the protagonist gain? What are its limits or costs? What result can other people see? What happens when the rule is made public, misunderstood or exploited? The first demonstration should solve one small problem, letting readers infer the rule from the result. If an on-screen interface appears, show only the current goal, constraint and result.

heading.zh: 用五方向测试长篇容量
heading.en: Test the Novel’s Capacity in Five Directions

body.zh:
同一规则至少尝试五种展开：**生计**改变钱与资源，**职业**改变资格与责任，**关系**改变信任与边界，**公共评价**改变旁人站队，**规则反噬**迫使主角换用法。五个方向应共享同一核心规则，却使用不同筹码和代价。

只能写出“奖励越来越大”，说明规则还没有故事容量；新增完全无关能力，又会让核心卖点失焦。
body.en:
Test the same rule in at least five directions: **livelihood**, changing money and resources; **work**, changing qualifications and responsibilities; **relationships**, changing trust and boundaries; **public opinion**, changing whom bystanders support; and **backlash from the rule**, forcing the protagonist to use it differently. All five directions should share the same core rule while using different leverage and costs.

If the only development you can imagine is “bigger and bigger rewards,” the rule does not yet have enough story capacity. Adding entirely unrelated powers will also blur the central appeal.

heading.zh: 原创范例：建议会留下回声
heading.en: Original Example: Advice That Leaves an Echo

body.zh:
失业的声音剪辑师顾南获得一种异常：任何人当面对他说出的建议，都会在次日变成一段只有他能听见的环境回声，但回声只保留说话者真正愿意承担的部分。

第一单元里，朋友劝他“随便接个活”，回声却只有沉默，顾南因此拒绝免费试做。第二单元，客户承诺承担版权责任，回声留下具体署名；顾南接受项目，却发现公开播放会让所有人短暂听见这些回声。

能力从求职判断扩展到合同、关系和公共评价，每次收益都伴随暴露风险。
body.en:
Gu Nan, an unemployed sound editor, develops an anomaly: any advice someone says to him face to face becomes an ambient echo the next day, audible only to him. But the echo retains only the part of the advice the speaker is genuinely willing to stand behind.

In the first story unit, a friend tells him to “just take any job.” The echo contains only silence, so Gu Nan refuses to do a free trial. In the second, a client promises to take responsibility for copyright. The echo preserves a specific promise of attribution. Gu Nan accepts the project, only to discover that public playback briefly lets everyone hear these echoes.

The ability expands from judging a job offer to dealing with contracts, relationships and public opinion. Each benefit comes with a risk of exposure.

heading.zh: 脑洞写到中段怎样防崩
heading.en: Keep the Speculative Premise from Collapsing Midway

body.zh:
追踪每次使用后谁知道规则、主角失去什么退路、现实身份如何变化。对手会学习，机构会形成新规则，亲友也会重新判断主角。让旧用法逐渐失效，主角必须改变策略。

常见失败包括连续贴面板、奖励只在数字上增长、现实人物只负责震惊、规则毫无代价。修正时把结果落到账单、合同、权限、关系决定或公开责任，并保留主角的主动选择。
body.en:
Track who knows the rule after each use, which options the protagonist has lost and how their real-world identity changes. Opponents learn; organisations create new rules; friends and family reassess the protagonist. Let earlier uses gradually stop working so the protagonist has to change strategy.

Common failures include displaying an interface in scene after scene, rewards growing only as numbers, ordinary characters reacting with shock but doing nothing else, and rules with no cost. Make outcomes affect bills, contracts, permissions, relationship decisions or public accountability while preserving the protagonist’s active choices.

q.zh: 需要按固定阶段或章节数写吗？
q.en: Do I need to use fixed phases or a fixed number of chapters?

a.zh: 不需要。阶段由人物取得的资源、权力、关系与选择发生了什么变化来划分。
a.en: No. Divide phases according to changes in the character’s resources, power, relationships and choices.

q.zh: 示例可以直接换名字使用吗？
q.en: Can I use the example by changing only the names?

a.zh: 示例用于说明方法。新故事应重新设计冲突发动机、人物选择、代价和兑现方式。
a.en: The example illustrates the method. A new story needs its own conflict engine, character choices, costs and payoffs.

title.zh: 短剧灯光提示词怎么写：从光源、职责到跨镜连续
title.en: Micro-Drama Lighting: Source, Narrative Job and Continuity

seo_title.zh: 短剧灯光提示词怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Micro-Drama Lighting: Source and Continuity | ZenStory

description.zh: 先确定本镜要看清或隐藏的信息，再把真实光源、方向、受光结果和背景分离写进提示词。附原创修表铺夜戏示例、可复制模板与跨镜纠错表。
description.en: Set shot intent: reveal or conceal; name source, direction, lit result and subject/background separation. Watch-repair example, template, continuity fixes.

answer.zh: 灯光提示词不要从“电影感”开始，而要先回答本镜需要看清什么、场景里什么在发光、光从哪边来、主体和背景如何分开。把光位术语与可见结果写在一起；连续场景保持光源关系，景别变化允许亮度自然变化。
answer.en: Do not start lighting prompts with “cinematic.” First decide what the shot must reveal, what is actually emitting light and where the light comes from. Describe lighting terms alongside visible results, including how the subject separates from the background. Keep light-source relationships consistent across a continuous scene while allowing brightness to change naturally with shot size.

heading.zh: 先定灯光的叙事职责
heading.en: Decide What the Lighting Needs to Tell

body.zh:
同一个房间不需要每镜都一样亮，但每镜都要服务当前信息。先把职责归到下表，再决定亮暗。

| 本镜职责 | 需要保住 | 可采用的光线选择 |
|---|---|---|
| 读表情 | 眼睛、嘴角或呼吸变化 | 面部保留层次，暗侧仍能辨认关键表演 |
| 看证据 | 物件形状、刻痕或文字 | 让证据与桌面产生局部对比，不必把全屋照亮 |
| 暂扣身份 | 轮廓存在，但脸不被认出 | 让人物落在暗区或形成剪影，同时守住既有光源方向 |
| 建立空间 | 门窗、通道和人物层次 | 用前后景亮度或色彩层级分开空间 |

“阴暗、氛围感强”没有说明观众该看哪里。先写职责，才能判断脸被压暗是设计还是错误。
body.en:
Brightness can vary from shot to shot in the same room; each shot should still serve the information being conveyed. Classify the job first, then decide how light or dark the image should be.

| Job of the shot | What must remain visible | Possible lighting choice |
|---|---|---|
| Read an expression | Eyes, the corner of a mouth or a change in breathing | Preserve facial shape; keep the key performance legible on the shadow side |
| See evidence | An object’s shape, engraving or writing | Create local contrast between the evidence and the tabletop without lighting the entire room |
| Withhold identity for now | A visible outline without a recognisable face | Place the figure in shadow or silhouette while preserving the established light-source direction |
| Establish space | Doors, windows, passageways and the characters’ depth | Separate layers of space through differences in brightness or colour |

“Dark, atmospheric lighting” does not tell the audience where to look. Decide the shot’s job first so you can tell whether a darkened face is intentional or a mistake.

heading.zh: 灯光提示词的可复制句式
heading.en: A Copyable Structure for Lighting Prompts

body.zh:
按这个顺序写：

> 场景事实：___是本镜实际光源，时段／开关状态为___。主光来自画面___侧。画面结果：___表面较亮，___留有___阴影，但___仍可辨认。注意中心：用___与背景分离。保持：相邻镜既有的光源方向与色调关系。不要：新增无来源光源，或让必须可读的___沉入黑暗。

“画面左侧”与“人物左侧”要写清是哪一种。只写“侧光”会留下方向歧义；只写“左侧来光”又没有说明脸、衣料和背景最终应怎样呈现。两者合写，执行与检查都有落点。
body.en:
Write in this order:

> **Scene facts:** ___ is the actual light source in this shot; time of day / switch state: ___. The key light comes from the ___ side of the frame. **Visible result:** ___ is brighter; ___ keeps a ___ shadow, but ___ remains legible. **Point of attention:** Separate ___ from the background using ___. **Maintain:** the light-source direction and colour relationship established in adjacent shots. **Avoid:** adding a source with no explanation, or losing ___ in darkness when it must remain readable.

Specify whether you mean screen left or the character’s left. “Side lighting” leaves the direction unclear; “light from the left” does not say how the face, fabric and background should look. Write both the direction and the result so the shot can be executed and checked.

heading.zh: 原创示例：深夜修表铺的一张保修单
heading.en: Original Example: A Warranty Slip in a Watch Shop at Night

body.zh:
场景：修表师温岑在打烊后的铺子里核对一张保修单。店内顶灯已经关闭，只剩工作台灯和街外招牌反光。学徒站在门边，暂时不知道单据上的签名是自己父亲。

**镜头一，先让证据可读**：中近景看温岑与工作台。提示写“暖色台灯位于画面右下方，保修单与温岑手指受光；她面向镜头的一侧脸颊有柔和亮度，眼睛可辨。门边学徒落在较暗的冷色招牌反光里，轮廓与门框分开，脸部细节暂不强调。”

**镜头二，注意转到学徒**：反打仍沿用台灯在空间中的位置，不把它搬到学徒正面。写“画面左后方的台灯余光勾出学徒靠近桌边后的手背；街外冷色反光保留在他脸侧，签名被念出后眼睛与停住的呼吸可辨。”

变化的是注意中心和取景，不是店里突然多了一盏灯。若第二镜为了“好看”变成均匀正面光，空间事实和揭示节奏都会断。
body.en:
Scene: After closing, watchmaker Wen Cen checks a warranty slip in her shop. The overhead light is off; only the workbench lamp and reflections from a sign outside remain. The apprentice stands near the door and does not yet know that the signature on the slip is his father’s.

**Shot 1 — Make the evidence legible:** A medium close shot of Wen Cen and the workbench. Prompt: “A warm bench lamp sits at the lower right of the frame, illuminating the warranty slip and Wen Cen’s fingers. The cheek facing camera has soft light; her eyes are legible. The apprentice by the door falls into cooler, dimmer reflected light, his outline separated from the doorframe; do not emphasise facial detail yet.”

**Shot 2 — Shift attention to the apprentice:** In the reverse shot, keep the lamp in the same place in the room; do not move it in front of the apprentice. Prompt: “Spill from the bench lamp at the back left of the frame catches the apprentice’s hand as he moves closer to the table. Cool reflections from the street remain along the side of his face. Once the signature is read aloud, his eyes and the tension around them remain visible as he holds his breath.”

The framing and point of attention change, not the number of lamps in the shop. If the second shot uses even frontal light just to look attractive, both the spatial facts and the timing of the reveal break.

heading.zh: 常见失败怎样改
heading.en: How to Fix Common Lighting-Prompt Failures

body.zh:
| 失败写法 | 为什么失效 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 电影感布光，质感高级 | 没有光源、方向或画面结果 | 写实际光源与必须读到的表面、脸或证据 |
| 所有人都有轮廓光 | 把一种效果当成默认配置 | 只有需要与背景分离时才写，且说明光从何处来 |
| 每镜亮度数值完全一致 | 景别和视角变化仍会改变画面亮度 | 保持光源关系与色调逻辑，比较可对应的脸、衣物和墙面 |
| 参考板很亮，所以夜戏也照亮 | 角色板照明只为看清形制 | 明确参考图管身份，本镜灯光按场景事实设计 |
| 为神秘感压黑全部脸 | 同时丢掉必须读的反应 | 指定哪张脸暂扣、哪项表演仍须可见 |
body.en:
| Weak prompt | Why it fails | Revision |
|---|---|---|
| Cinematic lighting, premium texture | Gives no source, direction or visible result | Name the actual source and the surface, face or evidence that must be readable |
| Everyone gets a rim light | Treats one effect as a default setting | Add it only when separation from the background is needed, and state where the light comes from |
| Use exactly the same brightness in every shot | Shot size and viewpoint still change perceived brightness | Preserve source relationships and colour logic; compare corresponding faces, clothing and walls |
| The reference board is bright, so light the night scene brightly too | Reference-character lighting exists to show design clearly | Specify that the reference controls identity, while the shot’s lighting follows the scene facts |
| Darken every face for mystery | Also hides reactions that need to be read | Specify whose identity is withheld and which performance must remain visible |

heading.zh: 从分镜到检查的四步
heading.en: Four Steps from Storyboard to Review

body.zh:
1. 圈出本镜唯一最重要的脸、动作或证据。
2. 从场景设定列出现有光源与开关状态，不临时造灯。
3. 写方向加结果，再写主体与背景如何分开。
4. 串看相邻镜：光源方向或剧情光态错了就回上游修；轻微曝光、白平衡差异才考虑后期校正。

需要生成提示时，把这一页的灯光句与人物、场景、动作要求合并；不要让一串灯光词盖住镜头职责。
body.en:
1. Circle the single most important face, action or piece of evidence in the shot.
2. List the existing light sources and switch states from the scene description; do not invent a lamp at the last minute.
3. State direction and visible result, then how the subject separates from the background.
4. Review adjacent shots together. If light direction or the story’s lighting state is wrong, fix it upstream. Reserve post-production correction for minor exposure or white-balance differences.

When generating a prompt, combine the lighting sentence with the character, scene and action requirements. Do not let a string of lighting terms obscure the shot’s purpose.

q.zh: 灯光提示词要写具体参数吗？
q.en: Do lighting prompts need specific technical settings?

a.zh: 没有已经接受的制作参数时，不必凭空写数值。先写可观察的光源、方向、明暗关系和可读结果；真实制作若有灯具或摄影参数，再按项目证据补充。
a.en: Not unless the production has already established technical settings. Start with observable light sources, direction, contrast and what must remain legible. Add fixture or camera settings only when the project provides evidence for them.

q.zh: 角色参考图的灯光要一直保持吗？
q.en: Must the lighting in a character reference image stay the same?

a.zh: 不用。参考板的均匀照明通常用于看清身份与造型；正式镜头的光按场景事实设计，同时保住需要识别的稳定特征。
a.en: No. Even lighting on a reference board is usually there to show identity and design clearly. Light the actual shot according to the scene facts while preserving the character features that need to remain recognisable.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-storyboard 为这组镜头设计灯光，先列每镜必须读清或暂扣的信息，再写实际光源、画面方向、受光结果和相邻镜连续性。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-storyboard`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /short-drama-storyboard to design lighting for these shots. First list what each shot must reveal or withhold, then specify the actual light source, direction in frame, visible result and continuity with adjacent shots.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.

title.zh: 镜头运动怎么设计：推拉摇移都要有叙事动机
title.en: Designing Camera Movement: Give Every Move a Story Motive

seo_title.zh: 镜头运动怎么设计｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Design Camera Movement | ZenStory

description.zh: 不按镜头轮流塞推拉摇移，而是从注意转移、压力变化和空间行动选择运镜。附原创失物招领处案例、运镜判断表和失败修正。
description.en: Choose camera moves for shifts in attention, pressure or space—not by rote. Includes a lost-property scene, movement checklist and fixes.

answer.zh: 镜头运动先回答“运动结束后，观众的注意、距离感或空间认识改变了什么”。摇镜适合把注意交给新对象，前移或后移改变亲近与压力，跟拍用于人物移动本身有策略意义的场面。没有变化时，固定机位往往更清楚。
answer.en: Before moving the camera, ask what changes in the audience’s attention, sense of distance or understanding of space by the end of the move. A pan can hand attention to a new object; a push or pull changes intimacy and pressure; tracking suits scenes where a character’s movement has strategic meaning. When nothing changes, a static camera is often clearer.

heading.zh: 先写变化，再选运镜名称
heading.en: Define the Change Before Naming a Camera Move

body.zh:
| 想让观众获得的变化 | 可考虑 | 不应自动使用 |
|---|---|---|
| 从说话者发现画外证据 | 摇镜或俯仰，把注意交过去 | 为了活泼无目标地左右摆动 |
| 更靠近一个无法回避的决定 | 缓慢前移 | 每句重话都机械推近 |
| 人物与关系突然疏远 | 后移或人物离机 | 仅用变焦替代真实空间变化 |
| 行走本身体现追赶、逃避或控制 | 跟拍 | 人物只是从门走到桌边也全程跟 |
| 原地关系被重新看懂 | 有理由的环绕 | 因为“高级感”绕人物一圈 |
| 让观众观察等待、受困或仪式 | 固定机位 | 害怕静止就补漂移 |

先写运动的终点信息。例如“摇到柜台下方露出一只仍在震动的手机”，比“镜头自然摇动”清楚；若摇完没有新事实，运动大概率可以删。
body.en:
| Change you want viewers to experience | Consider | Do not use automatically |
|---|---|---|
| Discover evidence outside the speaker’s eyeline | Shift attention to a defined point with a pan or tilt | Wandering side to side for energy without a target |
| Move closer to a decision that cannot be avoided | A slow push-in | Pushing closer mechanically on every serious line |
| Make a character or relationship suddenly feel more distant | Pull back or let the character move away from camera | Using a zoom as a substitute for an actual change in spatial relationships |
| Show pursuit, escape or control through the act of walking | Tracking | Following someone all the way from the door to the table when the walk has no strategy |
| Reframe an already established relationship | A motivated orbit | Circling a character just for a “premium” look |
| Let viewers observe waiting, confinement or ritual | A static camera | Adding drift because stillness feels uncomfortable |

First, write the information revealed at the end of the move. “Pan down to reveal a phone still vibrating beneath the counter” is clearer than “the camera pans naturally.” If the move reveals no new fact, it can probably be cut.

heading.zh: 四问决定移动还是切镜
heading.en: Four Questions: Move the Camera or Cut?

body.zh:
1. **新信息在同一空间内吗？** 在场内且需要保留连续关系，可以移动；跨时间地点则应按剪辑处理。
2. **过程重要还是结果重要？** 观众要看人物怎样逼近出口，跟随过程有意义；只需知道他已经到门口，可以在状态闭合处切。
3. **移动会不会抢走表演？** 长对白、精细手部动作和复杂运镜争夺同一时间时，先保故事动作。
4. **终点能否落住？** 运动到达后要给观众读信息的时间，不能在终点刚出现就立刻换动作。

决定一段移动后，用同一套连贯摄影机行为。不要同时写“固定机位、缓慢推进并跟随人物”，除非明确分成先后阶段。
body.en:
1. **Is the new information in the same space?** If it is in the scene and continuity matters, move the camera. If time or place changes, handle it as an edit.
2. **Does the process matter more than the result?** Follow a character approaching an exit if viewers need to see how they get there. If viewers only need to know they reached the door, cut once the action lands.
3. **Will the move compete with the performance?** When a long speech, precise hand action and elaborate camera move all demand the same moment, preserve the story action first.
4. **Can the ending composition settle?** Give viewers time to read the information after the camera arrives. Do not change the action the moment the destination appears.

Once you choose a move, describe one coherent camera behaviour. Do not write “static, slowly pushing in and following the character” at the same time unless you clearly divide it into sequential phases.

heading.zh: 原创示例：失物招领处的两把伞
heading.en: Original Example: Two Umbrellas at Lost Property

body.zh:
社区失物招领处，值班员叶明把一把黑伞递给来领伞的顾客。顾客展开伞，内侧却缝着幼儿园姓名贴；真正的伞仍靠在远处墙边。

- **开场固定中景**：柜台、两人和待领物架都在关系里，叶明递伞。此时不跟着手来回移动，让观众先看清错误交接。
- **摇镜有明确终点**：顾客说“这不是我的”，把伞内侧转向叶明。镜头从两人摇到姓名贴，让注意从争执转到证据；到达后停一拍。
- **后移改变认识**：叶明抬眼寻找，镜头随他的视线轻轻后移，把墙边另一把伞纳入同一空间。后移用于让观众发现解决线索一直在现场，不承担制造宏大感。
- **最后固定**：叶明没有立刻取伞，而是先核对登记本。固定机位让他的谨慎选择落住。

若全程用环绕，姓名贴、另一把伞与登记动作都会在运动中争抢注意；“镜头很忙”不等于场面更有张力。
body.en:
At a community lost-property desk, attendant Ye Ming hands a black umbrella to someone claiming it. The customer opens it; a kindergarten name label is sewn inside. The correct umbrella remains against the far wall.

- **Begin on a static medium shot:** Keep the desk, both people and the shelf of items in the same spatial relationship as Ye Ming hands over the umbrella. Do not chase the hands yet; let viewers first see the mistaken handoff.
- **Tilt to a defined endpoint:** The customer says, “This isn’t mine,” and turns the umbrella’s inside towards Ye Ming. Tilt down from the two people to the label, moving attention from their disagreement to the evidence. Hold when you arrive.
- **Pull back to change what viewers know:** Ye Ming looks up to search. Ease back with his eyeline to bring the other umbrella by the wall into the same frame. The pullback lets viewers discover the clue was present all along; it is not there to make the shot feel grand.
- **End static:** Ye Ming does not immediately take the umbrella. He checks the logbook first. A static camera lets the cautious choice register.

If the camera circles throughout, the label, the second umbrella and the logbook action all compete for attention. A busy camera does not automatically make a scene more tense.

heading.zh: 把运镜写成可执行句
heading.en: Write Camera Moves as Executable Instructions

body.zh:
> 起点：固定中景保持柜台两人关系。触发：顾客把伞内侧转向镜头，露出姓名贴。摄影机：沿她的动作向下轻摇，止于姓名贴清楚可读的构图。到达后：保持片刻，让叶明看清；不继续漂移，不改变伞的持有人。

一句有效运镜至少包括起点、触发、方向、终点信息和落住状态。若人物同时移动，再写清摄影机跟谁、与谁保持距离，以及运动结束时的空间关系。
body.en:
> **Start:** Static medium shot preserves the spatial relationship between the two people at the counter. **Trigger:** The customer turns the inside of the umbrella towards camera, revealing the name label. **Camera:** Tilt down gently with the movement and stop on a composition where the label is legible. **After arrival:** Hold briefly so Ye Ming can read it. Do not continue drifting or change who is holding the umbrella.

A useful camera instruction states at least the start, trigger, direction, information at the endpoint and how the shot settles. If a character also moves, say whom the camera follows, what distance it maintains and the spatial relationship at the end of the move.

heading.zh: 装饰性运镜的修正表
heading.en: A Troubleshooting Table for Decorative Camera Movement

body.zh:
| 症状 | 先问 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 每镜都缓慢推进 | 推近后关系变了吗 | 无变化就固定，或把推进留给真正无法回避的时刻 |
| 摇镜来回寻找 | 观众是否早已知道目标 | 已知对象可直接切或稳定构图，不重复搜索 |
| 跟拍人物做琐碎走动 | 走动本身有策略吗 | 删走动、固定观察，或只保留关键抵达 |
| 运镜与复杂动作同时发生 | 哪项是本镜主事件 | 简化摄影机，让动作因果清楚完成 |
| 环绕一圈回到原位 | 绕开后看到了什么新关系 | 没有新面或新处境就删掉环绕 |
body.en:
| Symptom | Ask first | Revision |
|---|---|---|
| Every shot slowly pushes in | Does the relationship change after the push? | If nothing changes, stay static; reserve the push for a moment that truly cannot be avoided |
| The camera pans back and forth searching | Do viewers already know what to look for? | If the object is already known, cut directly to it or hold a stable composition; do not repeat the search |
| The camera follows trivial walking | Does the walk itself have a strategy? | Remove the walk, observe statically or keep only the meaningful arrival |
| The camera moves during complex action | Which action is the main event of this shot? | Simplify the camera so the cause and effect of the action remain clear |
| An orbit circles back to the starting point | What new relationship becomes visible during the orbit? | Remove the orbit if it reveals no new side or situation |

q.zh: 推镜和变焦是一回事吗？
q.en: Are a dolly move and a zoom the same thing?

a.zh: 视觉效果可能都让主体变大，但空间感与关系变化不同。本文先解决叙事动机；具体器材或数字参数应按实际制作方案决定，不用术语替代终点信息。
a.en: They can both make the subject appear larger, but they change spatial perception and relationships differently. This article starts with narrative motivation. Choose specific equipment or numeric settings according to the actual production plan; jargon is not a substitute for stating what the camera move should reveal at its endpoint.

q.zh: 静态对话是不是一定很无聊？
q.en: Does a static dialogue scene have to be boring?

a.zh: 可以有张力。固定机位可以让等待、权力距离和微小反应更可读。对话是否有张力首先取决于人物选择与后果，不需要靠持续漂移补救。
a.en: No. A static frame can make waiting, power distance and small reactions easier to read. Tension in dialogue depends first on character choices and consequences; continuous camera drift is not needed to rescue it.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-storyboard 检查这场戏的摄影机行为；逐镜说明注意或关系发生了什么变化，再决定固定、摇、推拉、跟拍或切镜，并写清运动终点。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-storyboard`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /short-drama-storyboard to review the camera behaviour in this scene. For each shot, explain what changes in attention or relationships, then choose a static frame, pan, tilt, push, pull, tracking move or cut. Specify where each move ends.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.

title.zh: 正反打怎么拍不跳轴：轴线、视线与道具连续
title.en: Shot–Reverse-Shot Continuity: Track the Axis, Eyelines and Props

seo_title.zh: 正反打与180度轴线怎么用｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Shot–Reverse-Shot and the 180-Degree Rule | ZenStory

description.zh: 从人物连线、工作侧和画面方向设计正反打，并处理跨轴、第三人反应与道具状态。附原创验票口三人对话示例和检查表。
description.en: Plan the axis, camera side and screen direction. Track crossings, third-person reactions and props through a three-person ticket-gate scene and checklist.

answer.zh: 正反打先画出人物之间的轴线，选择摄影机工作的同一侧，再让双方视线方向互相对应。切镜时同时核对人物画面左右、目光、道具归属和前一镜终点。跨轴不是禁忌，但要用可见移动、中性镜头或重新建立空间，让观众知道关系怎样改变。
answer.en: Start shot–reverse-shot coverage by mapping the line between the characters, choosing one side for the camera and making their eyelines correspond. At each cut, check screen positions, gaze, prop ownership and the endpoint of the previous shot. Crossing the axis is allowed; use a visible move, a neutral angle or a new spatial establishing shot so viewers understand how the relationship has changed.

heading.zh: 先把轴线看成空间关系
heading.en: Treat the Axis as a Spatial Relationship

body.zh:
两人面对面时，连接两人的假想线就是常见轴线。摄影机在同一侧工作，甲在画面一边看向另一边，乙的反打方向与之相对，观众更容易相信他们在看彼此。

先记四项：

| 项目 | 记录示例 |
|---|---|
| 人物连线 | 售票员—乘客 |
| 工作侧 | 摄影机始终在检票桌靠候车厅一侧 |
| 画面方向 | 售票员画左望向右；乘客画右望向左 |
| 固定锚点 | 闸机在后景左，出口在后景右 |

“画面左”不是人物的左手。写道具动作时，两套方向要分开，否则反打后很容易出现同一张票突然换手。
body.en:
When two people face one another, the imagined line connecting them is a common axis. Keep the camera on the same side of that line and the eyelines tend to match: Character A looks from one side of the frame towards the other; the reverse shot of Character B looks back in the opposite screen direction. Viewers are more likely to believe the characters are looking at each other.

Record four things first:

| Item | Example |
|---|---|
| Line between characters | Ticket clerk — passenger |
| Camera side | Camera stays on the waiting-room side of the ticket desk |
| Screen direction | Clerk is frame-left looking right; passenger is frame-right looking left |
| Fixed anchors | Turnstile in the left background; exit in the right background |

“Frame-left” does not mean the character’s left hand. Keep frame direction and character-relative direction separate in prop instructions, or the same ticket may suddenly switch hands after a reverse cut.

heading.zh: 一组正反打至少要守住什么
heading.en: What a Shot–Reverse-Shot Setup Must Preserve

body.zh:
1. **建立关系**：先让观众知道双方和关键锚点的位置，无需固定使用大全景。
2. **对切有职责**：切给谁，是为了读新信息、决定或反应，不是每句台词自动切一次。
3. **目光互相成立**：人物看的方向、眼高和对象一致。
4. **动作只发生一次**：递票、收回、开门等状态变化归一个主要镜头；反打只承接结果或反应。
5. **第三人没有被忘掉**：他可留在同框、获得反应镜或被有意暂扣，但不能无缘无故消失。
body.en:
1. **Establish the relationship:** Let viewers understand where both people and key spatial anchors are. A wide shot is not mandatory.
2. **Give each cut a job:** Cut to someone to reveal new information, a decision or a reaction—not automatically after every line of dialogue.
3. **Make the eyelines meet:** Keep the direction, height and target of each character’s gaze consistent.
4. **Make each action happen once:** One principal shot owns a state change such as handing over a ticket, taking it back or opening a door. The reverse shot carries the result or reaction.
5. **Keep track of the third person:** They can remain in the frame, get a reaction shot or be deliberately withheld, but should not disappear without reason.

heading.zh: 原创示例：末班车验票口
heading.en: Original Example: The Last Train’s Ticket Gate

body.zh:
末班车前，乘客周茵把纸票递给售票员曹川。保安站在闸机内侧，手里拿着关闭通道的牌子。曹川发现票上日期是明天，但周茵说手机通知就是今晚。

| 镜头 | 机位与画面 | 连续性职责 |
|---|---|---|
| 建立镜 | 检票桌斜侧中景，曹川画左、周茵画右，保安在后景闸机旁 | 建立轴线、闸机与第三人；票仍在周茵右手 |
| 曹川反打 | 同一工作侧，中近景，视线朝画右 | 周茵把票递入画，曹川接住；票的状态在本镜变为曹川持有 |
| 周茵反打 | 同侧中近景，视线朝画左 | 她举起手机解释，双手不再持票；不要再演一次递票 |
| 保安反应 | 回到能看见闸机的角度 | 他暂缓放下关闭牌，让争议产生后果 |

如果周茵反打中票又回到她手里，问题不只是“跳轴”，而是动作状态被重置。空间方向和物件连续要一起查。
body.en:
Before the last train, passenger Zhou Yin hands a paper ticket to ticket clerk Cao Chuan. A security guard stands inside the turnstile holding a “PASSAGE CLOSED” sign. Cao Chuan notices the ticket is dated for tomorrow, but Zhou Yin says the notification on her phone says tonight.

| Shot | Position and image | Continuity job |
|---|---|---|
| Establishing shot | Angled medium shot from the ticket-desk side: Cao Chuan frame-left, Zhou Yin frame-right, guard beside the turnstile in the background | Establish axis, turnstile and third person; ticket remains in Zhou Yin’s right hand |
| Cao Chuan’s reverse | Medium close shot from the same camera side, eyeline towards frame-right | Zhou Yin passes the ticket into frame and Cao Chuan takes it; ownership changes in this shot |
| Zhou Yin’s reverse | Medium close shot from the same side, eyeline towards frame-left | She raises her phone to explain and no longer holds the ticket; do not perform the handoff again |
| Guard’s reaction | Return to an angle that shows the turnstile | He delays putting the “PASSAGE CLOSED” sign in place, so the dispute has a consequence |

If the ticket is back in Zhou Yin’s hand in her reverse shot, the problem is not only crossing the axis: the prop’s state has been reset. Check spatial direction and object continuity together.

heading.zh: 什么时候可以跨轴，怎样让观众跟上
heading.en: When and How to Cross the Axis

body.zh:
跨轴本身不是错误。人物绕过桌子、权力位置翻转，或主观混乱确有意义时，可以改变工作侧。常见做法：

- 同一镜内拍到人物或摄影机穿过轴线，让改变可见；
- 先给接近轴线的中性角度，再在另一侧建立新关系；
- 用一镜重新交代人物与固定锚点，然后开始新的对切；
- 有意制造迷失时，也要确认观众丢失方向正是设计，而非偶然。

不要只在剪辑点把两人左右突然互换，然后靠台词让观众猜。跨轴之后重新记录新的画面方向与道具状态。
body.en:
Crossing the axis is not inherently wrong. You may change the camera side when a character walks around a desk, a power relationship flips or subjective disorientation serves the scene. Common ways to make the change legible include:

- Show the character or camera crossing the line within one shot.
- Use a neutral angle close to the axis, then establish the new relationship from the other side.
- Re-establish the characters and fixed spatial anchors in one shot before beginning a new shot–reverse-shot pattern.
- If you deliberately disorient viewers, confirm that losing their sense of direction is the intention rather than an accident.

Do not suddenly swap the characters’ left-right positions only at the edit and expect dialogue to explain it. After crossing, record the new screen directions and prop states.

heading.zh: 正反打剪在一起后的检查清单
heading.en: A Continuity Checklist for Edited Shot–Reverse-Shot

body.zh:
- [ ] 双方是在看彼此，还是看画外第三个对象？
- [ ] 眼高、视线方向和人物位置能否对应？
- [ ] 前镜终点的手、道具、坐姿是否成为后镜起点？
- [ ] 每次切镜是否增加反应、证据或新理解？
- [ ] 第三人仍在场时，他的在场状态是否有安排？
- [ ] 若跨轴，观众是否看到了穿越或重新建立空间？

发现左右混乱时，不要先给镜头加更多运动。回到建立镜和状态表，找出从哪一镜开始关系失真。
body.en:
- [ ] Are the characters looking at each other, or at a third person off-screen?
- [ ] Do their eyeline heights, gaze directions and positions correspond?
- [ ] Do the hands, props and seated positions at the previous shot’s endpoint match the next shot’s start?
- [ ] Does every cut add a reaction, evidence or new understanding?
- [ ] If the third person is present, is their status in the scene accounted for?
- [ ] If the axis is crossed, do viewers see the crossing or a new spatial setup?

When screen directions become confusing, do not start by adding more camera movement. Return to the establishing shot and the state record to find where the spatial relationship first drifted.

q.zh: 正反打一定要先拍全景吗？
q.en: Does shot–reverse-shot always require a wide establishing shot first?

a.zh: 不要求大全景。关键是观众能建立人物、锚点与工作侧。一个能清楚呈现双方和关键空间的中景也可以承担建立职责。
a.en: No. Viewers need to understand the characters, spatial anchors and camera side. A medium shot that clearly shows both people and the important space can establish the scene.

q.zh: 故意跳轴可以制造紧张吗？
q.en: Can a deliberate axis-crossing create tension?

a.zh: 可以有意改变方向，但应有明确叙事目的，并让观众能理解改变或确实需要迷失。无动机的左右互换通常只会让人物关系和动作状态难读。
a.en: Yes, if the change has a clear narrative purpose and viewers can understand it—or are meant to feel disoriented. An unmotivated left-right swap usually just makes the relationships and action harder to follow.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-storyboard 为这段对话设计正反打，先标人物连线、工作侧、画面方向和固定锚点，再检查每镜视线、第三人反应及道具起终状态。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-storyboard`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /short-drama-storyboard to design shot–reverse-shot coverage for this dialogue. First mark the line between the characters, camera side, screen directions and fixed anchors. Then check eyelines, third-person reactions and the starting and ending state of each prop.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.

title.zh: 短剧声音怎么设计：让环境声、留白与声音桥推动剧情
title.en: Micro-Drama Sound: Ambience, Silence and Sound Bridges

seo_title.zh: 短剧声音设计与沉默戏怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Micro-Drama Sound Design and Silence | ZenStory

description.zh: 声音设计不等于罗列音效。先确定声源怎样建立空间、施加压力、让路给证据，再安排撤出、恢复与声音桥。附原创自助洗衣店案例。
description.en: Assign sound a dramatic job: establish space, apply pressure, yield to evidence, then withdraw or return. Includes an original laundromat scene.

answer.zh: 短剧声音设计要从场次作用出发：开场由什么声音建立空间，哪个声源代表秩序或压力，哪句台词或选择前需要主动留白，声音何时因可见事件撤出、恢复或改变距离。沉默需要明确让哪些声音退开、给什么信息让路、何时回来，不能只漏写音轨。
answer.en: Design sound around the job of each scene: which sound establishes the space, which source represents order or pressure, and where to deliberately leave room before a line or choice? Decide when sound withdraws, returns or changes distance in response to visible events. Silence requires specifying which sounds recede, what they make room for and when they return; it is not simply a missing track.

heading.zh: 先给声音分配戏剧职责
heading.en: Give Sound a Dramatic Job

body.zh:
| 职责 | 写作问题 |
|---|---|
| 建立空间 | 观众先听见什么，能判断声源远近或画外存在吗 |
| 建立秩序 | 哪个反复声代表日常流程、权力或人物习惯 |
| 提供证据 | 哪个声音会改变人物或观众的判断 |
| 施加压力 | 声音怎样靠近、持续、被遮住或突然停止 |
| 主动留白 | 哪些声源退开，让台词、呼吸、物件或选择被听见 |
| 连接场次 | 前场声音如何带入下一场，又不提前泄露信息 |

空调、车流、鸟鸣不必每场列一遍。只有改变注意、空间感或人物压力的声音，才值得成为剧本里的事件。
body.en:
| Job | Question to answer |
|---|---|
| Establish space | What does the audience hear first? Can they judge the source’s distance or presence off-screen? |
| Establish order | Which recurring sound represents a routine, authority or a character’s habit? |
| Provide evidence | Which sound changes a character’s or viewer’s judgment? |
| Apply pressure | Does the sound approach, persist, become muffled or stop suddenly? |
| Deliberately leave space | Which sources recede so dialogue, breathing, an object or a choice can be heard? |
| Connect scenes | How can a sound carry into the next scene without revealing too much too early? |

You do not need to list air conditioning, traffic and birds in every scene. Only give a sound its own script event when it changes attention, spatial perception or pressure on a character.

heading.zh: 沉默戏要写“谁让路给谁”
heading.en: In a Silence, Specify What Gives Way to What

body.zh:
“全场安静”往往过于笼统。现实中的沉默可以分层：近处人先停话，远处机器仍运转；配乐撤出，但鞋底摩擦和吞咽变得清楚；一个角色故意继续制造噪声，掩饰自己已经听懂。

可复制句式：

> 当___发生后，___声逐渐／立即撤出，保留___作为空间底层；留白让___被听见。直到___这个可见事件发生，___声恢复／改变距离。

这里必须有触发与恢复条件。只写“停顿三秒”没有说明停掉什么，也没有说明这段空白为何存在。
body.en:
“The whole place goes silent” is often too vague. Silence in a real space can be layered: people nearby stop talking while distant machinery continues; music drops out while shoes scrape and someone swallows; a character deliberately makes noise to hide that they have understood.

**Reusable structure:**

> After ___ happens, the sound of ___ gradually / immediately withdraws, leaving ___ as the spatial bed. This space lets ___ be heard. When the visible event ___ happens, the sound of ___ returns / changes distance.

Specify what triggers the withdrawal and what allows sound to return. “Pause for three seconds” does not say what stops or why the gap exists.

heading.zh: 原创示例：午夜自助洗衣店
heading.en: Original Example: A Laundromat at Midnight

body.zh:
店主程鸢准备关门，最后一位顾客戴宁坚持等烘干机结束。滚筒里却传出一枚金属物反复撞击的声音；戴宁说口袋里没有东西。

1. **开场秩序**：只有戴宁面前的一台烘干机仍在低频运转，其余机器已经停下，规律的滚筒声充满临关门的店面。
2. **异常出现**：这台机器每转一圈响一次金属撞击。不加通用“悬疑音效”；让既有机器声里出现可定位的差异。
3. **主动留白**：程鸢按下这台机器的暂停键。滚筒声撤出，保留街外远处车辆；金属物最后滚落一下。这个留白让两人确认物件确实在机器里。
4. **人物分层**：程鸢不说话，戴宁却连续整理桌上的衣架，用塑料碰撞声遮住自己的紧张。
5. **恢复条件**：程鸢打开门、取出一枚陌生钥匙后，不立即恢复机器声；等戴宁承认衣服不是自己的，程鸢关好机门，重新启动这台机器。

声音的开始、撤出和恢复都跟可见行动相连。若用一声通用“惊吓冲击”盖住金属落地，真正的证据反而难以听清。
body.en:
Owner Cheng Yuan is about to close the laundromat. The last customer, Dai Ning, insists on waiting for a dryer cycle to finish. Something metal keeps knocking inside the drum. Dai Ning says there is nothing in their pocket.

1. **Opening order:** Only the dryer in front of Dai Ning is still running, with a low-frequency rumble. The other machines have stopped, leaving the regular drum rhythm to fill the shop as it prepares to close.
2. **The anomaly appears:** This machine makes one metallic knock on every rotation. Do not add a generic “suspense effect”; make the difference audible within the existing machine sound.
3. **Deliberately leave space:** Cheng Yuan presses pause on this dryer. The drum sound drops out, leaving distant traffic outside. The metal object gives one final roll. This gap lets both characters confirm that something is inside the machine.
4. **Different character layers:** Cheng Yuan says nothing. Dai Ning keeps rearranging hangers on the table, using the plastic clatter to conceal their nerves.
5. **Condition for return:** Cheng Yuan opens the door and removes an unfamiliar key. Do not immediately restore the machine sound. Wait until Dai Ning admits the clothes are not theirs; Cheng Yuan closes the dryer and starts it again.

The start, withdrawal and return of each sound are tied to visible actions. If a generic “shock hit” covers the metal object’s final roll, the evidence becomes harder to hear.

heading.zh: 声音桥怎样连接场景而不剧透
heading.en: Use Sound Bridges to Connect Scenes Without Spoilers

body.zh:
声音桥可以让前一场结果进入下一场。例如上一场以洗衣店机器重新启动结束，下一场先听见规律滚筒声，再出现另一处清晨洗衣房的画面，能形成节奏或主题连接。

但若下一场地点尚未允许揭示，不要提前使用只能指向那个地点的专属广播或人物声音。声音桥也不能凭空新增不存在的声源。先确认剧本里的信息权限和空间来源，再决定声音是持续、改变距离，还是在切点主动断开。
body.en:
A sound bridge can carry a result from one scene into the next. For example, the previous scene ends as a laundromat machine starts again. Viewers hear the regular drum rhythm before seeing an early-morning laundry room elsewhere, creating a rhythmic or thematic link.

If the next location is not yet meant to be revealed, do not play an announcement or a person’s voice that points only to that location. A sound bridge must not conjure a source that does not exist in the script. Check who can know what and where each sound comes from before deciding whether it continues, changes distance or stops at the cut.

heading.zh: 常见失败与修正
heading.en: Common Sound Problems and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 每镜都列完整环境音 | 按整场设计进入、撤出、恢复和转向，逐镜只落实变化 |
| 所有转折都加冲击音 | 优先让证据本身、人物动作或留白承担转折 |
| 配乐一停就叫沉默 | 写清仍保留的空间声，以及留白给谁让路 |
| 静音期间人物表演空白 | 配合目光、呼吸、停手或选择，让声音不替代表演 |
| 下一场声音提前透露身份 | 换成不越过信息权限的共同声源，或取消声音桥 |
body.en:
| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Listing complete ambience in every shot | Design entrance, withdrawal, return and shifts across the whole scene; specify only changes shot by shot |
| Adding an impact sound to every turn | Let the evidence itself, a character’s action or a deliberate gap carry the turn first |
| Calling it silence whenever music stops | Specify which spatial sounds remain and what the gap makes room for |
| Characters stop performing when sound drops | Use eyelines, breath, still hands or choices; sound must not replace performance |
| The next scene’s sound reveals an identity too early | Choose a shared source that respects information boundaries, or drop the bridge |

q.zh: 沉默戏需要完全没有声音吗？
q.en: Does a silence scene need to have no sound at all?

a.zh: 不需要。主动留白常常只是撤掉占据注意的声源，保留空间底声、呼吸或关键物件声。重点是让什么退开、让什么被听见。
a.en: No. Deliberately leaving space often means removing only the sound source that is occupying attention while preserving the room tone, breathing or a key object sound. The point is to say what recedes and what becomes audible.

q.zh: 剧本阶段要写混音参数吗？
q.en: Should I specify mixing parameters at the script stage?

a.zh: 本文聚焦故事需要的声音事实与进入退出关系，不凭空写后期参数。具体音量、压低和混音处理应在已有素材与制作方案上决定并试听。
a.en: This article focuses on the sound facts the story requires and on when sounds enter and exit; it does not invent post-production settings. Decide exact levels, ducking and mix treatment from the available material and production plan, then listen to the result.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-write 为这场戏设计场次级声音：先列开场声、秩序声、证据声、留白对象、恢复条件与可能的声音桥，不新增剧本里不存在的声源。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-write`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use /short-drama-write to design sound at the scene level. First list the opening sound, the sound of order, evidence sounds, what recedes for silence, the return condition and any possible sound bridge. Do not add a sound source that is not in the script.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-write`.

title.zh: 短剧台词节奏怎么设计：对白、动作与反应一起排
title.en: How to Time Short-Drama Dialogue with Action and Reaction

seo_title.zh: 短剧台词节奏与对话停顿怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Time Short-Drama Dialogue and Pauses | ZenStory

description.zh: 把完整台词、动作、打断、停顿和听者反应排在同一时间线上。附原创复印店争执案例、相对节拍模板与超载修正。
description.en: Map every line, action, interruption, pause, and listener reaction on a timeline. Includes a copy-shop example, relative-beat template, and overload fixes.

answer.zh: 短剧台词节奏要安排谁先听见、何时开口、哪些动作能与说话并行、哪些必须等上一句结束，以及结尾给谁的反应。没有真实录音时用“开口前、话音落下后、结尾停留”等相对节拍；容量不够就简化无关动作、拆镜或修订剧本，不静默删词。
answer.en: To time dialogue in a short drama, decide who hears first, when each person begins speaking, which actions can run alongside a line, which must wait until the previous line ends, and whose reaction closes the shot. Without a real recording, use relative beats such as “before the line,” “after the final word,” and “hold on the final reaction.” If the shot lacks capacity, simplify unrelated action, split the shot, or revise the script; never silently delete words.

heading.zh: 先分清句子写法与时间安排
heading.en: Separate Sentence Craft from Timing

body.zh:
台词内容解决人物说什么、为什么这样说；台词节奏解决这些话与动作在什么时候发生。排一段对话时同时看四层：

| 层 | 要记录 |
|---|---|
| 发声 | 完整原句、说话者、画内／画外 |
| 接收 | 谁先听懂，谁晚半拍，谁故意不回应 |
| 动作 | 哪个能边说边做，哪个必须等话说完 |
| 落点 | 句尾后留下什么反应或新状态 |

不要给每句都补同样长的停顿。停顿来自人物处理信息、掩饰、等待回答或做决定，不是统一标点。
body.en:
Dialogue content determines what a character says and why they say it. Dialogue timing determines when those words and accompanying actions happen. Track four layers while arranging an exchange:

| Layer | What to record |
|---|---|
| Voice | The complete original line, speaker, and whether the voice is on- or off-screen |
| Reception | Who understands first, who reacts a beat late, and who deliberately does not respond |
| Action | Which action can occur during speech and which must wait until the line ends |
| Landing point | What reaction or new state remains after the final word |

Do not add the same-length pause after every line. A pause comes from processing information, concealing a reaction, waiting for an answer, or making a decision; it is not uniform punctuation.

heading.zh: 没有实测音频时，用相对节拍
heading.en: Use Relative Beats When You Have No Measured Audio

body.zh:
可先这样写：

> 开头保留一拍：甲仍在完成___。
> 触发后：乙开口说完整原句___，同时只进行可并行的___。
> 话音落下后：甲先___，再回答___。
> 结尾：保留甲／乙的___反应，落到___状态。

相对节拍给表演与剪辑留出弹性。只有项目真的需要精确时间、且镜长已经接受时，才把阶段写成秒段；各段应覆盖完整时长，不能超出，也不能留一截让执行端自行填动作。
body.en:
Start with a template like this:

> Hold one beat at the opening: A is still finishing ___.
> After the trigger: B speaks the complete line ___ while performing only the parallel action ___.
> After B finishes: A first ___, then answers ___.
> At the end: hold on A’s/B’s ___ reaction, landing on the state ___.

Relative beats leave flexibility for performance and editing. Convert the phases into timed seconds only when the project truly needs precise timing and the shot length is already accepted. Those phases must cover the entire duration without exceeding it or leaving an unused fragment for production to fill with invented action.

heading.zh: 原创示例：复印店里的一页空白
heading.en: Original Example: A Blank Page at the Copy Shop

body.zh:
实习生林琅要在截止前复印申请表，店员于莱发现原件第二页是空白。林琅坚持说导师已经签过。关键是让“空白页”逐步改变两人的行动，而非赶完三句对白。

**原句**：

> 林琅：老师签过了，你先复印。
> 于莱：签名在哪一页？
> 林琅：第二页。

**节奏安排**：开头于莱不说话，先把第二页翻到正面并停住。林琅看到她停手后说第一句，边说边把零钱推过去；推零钱能与说话并行。于莱没有接钱，等第一句结束才把空白页转向林琅，问“签名在哪一页？”林琅先低头确认，再答“第二页”；回答后手指从零钱上收回。结尾留给于莱把两页对齐、暂不启动机器。

若于莱在林琅第一句中途就问，同时又翻页、接钱、按机器，信息与动作会互相遮挡。简化到“转页—问—认出—停机”，节奏反而更有压力。
body.en:
Intern Lin Lang needs to copy an application before the deadline. Clerk Yu Lai discovers that page two of the original is blank. Lin Lang insists that the adviser already signed it. The goal is to let the blank page change both characters’ actions step by step, not to rush through three lines.

**Original lines**:

> Lin Lang: My adviser signed it. Just make the copy.
> Yu Lai: Which page has the signature?
> Lin Lang: Page two.

**Timing**: At the opening, Yu Lai says nothing. She turns page two face up and stops. Once Lin Lang sees her stop, Lin speaks the first line while pushing some change across the counter; pushing the coins can run in parallel with the line. Yu Lai does not take the money. She waits for the line to end, turns the blank page toward Lin Lang, and asks, “Which page has the signature?” Lin Lang looks down to check before answering, “Page two.” After the answer, Lin’s fingers withdraw from the coins. The ending holds on Yu Lai aligning the two pages without starting the machine.

If Yu Lai asks midway through Lin Lang’s first line while also turning the page, taking the money, and pressing the machine controls, information and action obscure one another. Reducing the sequence to “turn the page, ask, recognize, do not start the machine” creates more pressure.

heading.zh: 对白放不下时，按这个顺序修
heading.en: When the Dialogue Does Not Fit, Revise in This Order

body.zh:
1. 删除没有故事作用的摸杯子、走动和环境忙碌。
2. 把能自然并行的轻动作与说话重叠，但不压缩互为条件的事件。
3. 保留完整台词和听者必须出现的反应。
4. 在语义与状态闭合处拆镜，或请求延长镜头。
5. 若确实要改词，回到剧本层修订，不在视频提示里自行删字。

拿到对应原句且语言、演法一致的录音后，按真实开口到收声的区间安排；没有就标“文本估计”，不要假称试听或用统一每秒字数保证容量。
body.en:
1. Remove cup-touching, walking, and background busyness that serves no story purpose.
2. Overlap light actions with speech where they fit naturally, but do not compress events that depend on one another.
3. Preserve every complete line and each listener reaction the scene requires.
4. Split the shot where meaning and state reach closure, or request a longer shot.
5. If the words truly must change, revise them at the script level instead of deleting them inside a video prompt.

Once you have a recording of the corresponding lines with matching language and performance, time the scene from the real onset of speech to the end of the voice. Without that recording, label the timing “estimated from text.” Do not claim to have listened or use one fixed characters-per-second rate as a guarantee of capacity.

heading.zh: 打断、抢话与沉默怎样写清
heading.en: How to Write Interruptions, Overlap, and Silence Clearly

body.zh:
- **打断**：写明被打断的原句停在哪里、谁因什么触发开口，以及前句是否以后续方式继续。
- **抢话**：两人可能短暂重叠，但要说明哪句话必须被听清，不能用“同时激烈争吵”代替内容。
- **沉默**：写处理对象和外显动作，例如听见名字后不回答，先把门卡翻到背面。
- **改称呼**：若称呼变化是关系转折，让听者反应占到时间，不要紧接下一句把它淹没。

最终检查整段时，不只听说话者，也看听者是否有时间接收。对白结束但镜头没有落点，是常见的“台词说完了，戏没演完”。
body.en:
- **Interruption**: State where the interrupted line stops, what triggers the other person to speak, and whether the first line continues later in another form.
- **Talking over someone**: Two voices may overlap briefly, but identify which words must remain intelligible. “They argue heatedly at the same time” is not a substitute for content.
- **Silence**: Name what the character is processing and the visible action it produces—for example, after hearing a name, they do not answer and instead turn a keycard facedown.
- **A changed form of address**: If a new name or title marks a relationship turn, give the listener’s reaction time instead of burying it beneath the next line.

In the final check, do not listen only to the speaker; make sure the listener has time to receive the line. Dialogue that ends without a visual landing point creates a common problem: the words are finished, but the scene is not.

q.zh: 短剧台词是不是越短越好？
q.en: Should every line in a short drama be as short as possible?

a.zh: 不是。句长要服务人物策略和当前容量。能删的是无作用的重复说明；人物必须完整表达的拒绝、条件或转折不能为了短而被改掉。
a.en: No. Line length should serve the character’s strategy and the available capacity. Cut repetitive explanation that does no work; do not shorten a refusal, condition, or turn that the character must express completely.

q.zh: 停顿要不要都标具体秒数？
q.en: Should every pause be marked in exact seconds?

a.zh: 通常先用相对节拍更实用。只有镜长和声音依据足够明确时再标秒段；真实生成或录音后还需回听完整性与节奏。
a.en: Usually, relative beats are more useful first. Add timed segments only when the shot length and audio basis are clear enough. After real generation or recording, listen back for completeness and rhythm.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中说：“用 /short-drama-video-prompts 为这镜对白排相对节拍，保留逐字台词，区分可并行动作与顺序动作，并为听者反应和结尾状态留出空间；容量不足时提出拆镜或修订。”Codex 中使用 `$short-drama-video-prompts`。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/short-drama-video-prompts` to arrange relative beats for the dialogue in this shot. Preserve every line word for word, distinguish parallel actions from sequential actions, and leave room for the listener’s reaction and the ending state. If the shot lacks capacity, propose splitting the shot or revising the script.” In Codex, use `$short-drama-video-prompts`.

title.zh: AI短剧参考图怎么用：角色、场景、构图与风格分开绑定
title.en: AI Short-Drama Image Roles: Character, Setting, Composition & Style

seo_title.zh: AI短剧参考图怎么用｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: AI Short-Drama Reference Images | ZenStory

description.zh: 一张参考图只控制明确职责，避免角色图越权改变服装、场景或构图。附九类参考职责、原创海岸气象站案例与冲突修正表。
description.en: Set roles so references cannot override wardrobe, setting or composition. Nine roles, an original coastal weather-station example and conflict fixes.

answer.zh: AI短剧使用参考图时，要为每张图写清“这次参考什么”和“哪些内容不能跟着变”。角色身份、临时造型、场景地理、构图、尺度、效果、起始帧、结束帧与风格是不同职责；同一张图承担两个职责时也要分开说明边界，不能写成“全参考”。
answer.en: When using reference images for AI short dramas, state what each image should inform this time and what must not change with it. Identity, temporary appearance, setting geography, composition, scale, effects, opening frame, closing frame and style are different roles. Even when one image serves two roles, state each boundary separately; never say “use it as a reference for everything.”

heading.zh: 为什么“参考这张图”容易失控
heading.en: Why “Use This Image as a Reference” Can Go Wrong

body.zh:
一张图同时包含脸、衣服、姿势、背景、文字和光线。只说“照着这张图”，下游无法知道哪些是必须保留的身份特征，哪些只是拍摄当时的偶然内容。结果可能是为了保住脸，连不该出现的外套、背景招牌和构图一起继承。

每张参考至少回答：它是谁／画什么、这次承担什么职责、允许控制哪些可见内容、哪些内容绝不能跟着变。文件存在不等于已经看过；没有获准观察时，应把水印、文字和裁切风险标为未验证。
body.en:
One image may contain a face, clothing, pose, background, text and lighting. If you only say “follow this image,” the next person or tool cannot tell which features must remain as identity anchors and which are incidental to that particular shot. The result may preserve the face but also carry over an unwanted coat, background sign or composition.

For every reference, state: what or who it depicts, the role it serves this time, which visible details it may control, and which details must not carry over. A file’s existence does not mean it has been inspected. Without authorization to inspect it, mark watermark, text and cropping risks as unverified.

heading.zh: 九类常用参考职责
heading.en: Nine Common Reference-Image Roles

body.zh:
| 职责 | 可以控制 | 默认不该控制 |
|---|---|---|
| 身份 | 脸型、体态、稳定识别点 | 临时姿势、场景、文字 |
| 造型状态 | 本场服装、湿污、伤损 | 新身份、背景方位 |
| 地理 | 入口、区域、固定锚点 | 临时人物与剧情状态 |
| 构图 | 占画比例、视线布局、留白 | 人物身份、服装 |
| 尺度 | 主体之间的相对大小 | 数量、动作结果、风格 |
| 效果 | 已决定效果的形态与范围 | 非目标对象的消失或变形 |
| 起始帧 | 本镜开始时的构图和状态 | 尚未发生的动作终点 |
| 结束帧 | 已写明的镜头终点 | 新剧情结果 |
| 风格 | 色彩、材质、阴影边缘、景深倾向 | 身份、地理、剧情与道具文字 |

角色本集始终不变的造型可以与身份一起记录；本集中会换装、淋湿或破损的状态应单独绑定，避免旧状态粘到后续镜头。
body.en:
| Role | May control | Should not control by default |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Face shape, build and stable identifying features | Temporary pose, setting, text |
| Appearance state | This scene’s clothing, wetness or damage | A new identity, background geography |
| Geography | Entrances, zones and fixed spatial anchors | Temporary characters and story state |
| Composition | Frame occupancy, eyeline layout and negative space | Character identity, clothing |
| Scale | Relative size between subjects | Count, action outcome, style |
| Effect | The form and extent of an already chosen effect | Disappearance or distortion of unrelated subjects |
| Opening frame | Composition and state at the start of this shot | The endpoint of an action that has not happened yet |
| Closing frame | A stated endpoint of the shot | A new story outcome |
| Style | Color relationships, material, shadow edges and depth-of-field tendencies | Identity, geography, story, or text on props |

If a character’s look stays the same throughout this episode, it can be recorded with identity. A changing state, such as a different outfit, wetness or damage, should be bound separately so an old state does not carry into later shots.

heading.zh: 可复制的参考图职责卡
heading.en: A Reusable Reference-Image Role Card

body.zh:
> 参考名称／定位：___
> 本次职责：身份／造型状态／地理／构图／尺度／效果／起始帧／结束帧／风格
> 允许控制：___
> 不得控制：___
> 观察状态：已获准看见并记录___／仅有创作者说明___／未验证
> 与其他参考冲突时优先保留：___

若同一图片既提供人物身份又提供构图，写两张职责卡：身份卡只管认人，构图卡只管画面布局。分开后才能在更换构图时继续保住角色，也能在更换角色时复用合理布局。
body.en:
**Reference name / location:** ___  
**Role this time:** identity / appearance state / geography / composition / scale / effect / opening frame / closing frame / style  
**May control:** ___  
**Must not control:** ___  
**Inspection status:** authorized and observed: ___ / creator’s description only: ___ / unverified  
**If references conflict, preserve first:** ___

If the same image provides both identity and composition, write two role cards: the identity card is only for recognizing the character; the composition card is only for the frame layout. Separating them lets you change the composition while keeping the character, or reuse a suitable layout with a different character.

heading.zh: 原创示例：海岸气象站的三张参考图
heading.en: Original Example: Three References at a Coastal Weather Station

body.zh:
镜头内容：新来的观测员许岚在夜班室发现风速记录纸被撕掉一角，随后走到窗前查看外面的测风塔。

| 参考图 | 本次职责 | 允许控制 | 不得控制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 许岚角色板 | 身份 | 短卷发、眉骨轮廓、体态与稳定工牌形制 | 角色板中的白天背景、站姿和均匀棚拍光 |
| 气象站平面／地点图 | 地理 | 门、记录桌、窗与塔的方向关系 | 临时人物、夜间表演和纸张破损状态 |
| 已接受夜海视觉样张 | 风格 | 冷暖层级、潮湿材质、阴影边缘 | 许岚的脸、室内窗位、记录纸文字 |

本镜起始帧另写“记录纸仍在桌上、缺角已经存在、许岚尚未走到窗边”。风格样张里若有另一名穿雨衣的人，不能因为“参考风格”把他带进气象站；角色板里的明亮背景也不能覆盖夜班室的场景光。
body.en:
**Shot:** New observer Xu Lan discovers that one corner of the wind-record sheet has been torn away in the night-shift room, then walks to the window to check the anemometer tower outside.

| Reference image | Role this time | May control | Must not control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Xu Lan’s character sheet | Identity | Short wavy hair, brow shape, build and the stable design of the name badge | The character-sheet’s daytime background, standing pose and even studio lighting |
| Weather-station floor plan / location image | Geography | The relative positions of the door, record desk, window and tower | Temporary characters, night performance and the torn-paper state |
| Approved night-sea visual sample | Style | Warm/cool balance, damp materials and shadow edges | Xu Lan’s face, the indoor window position, or text on the record sheet |

Describe the opening frame separately: “The record sheet is still on the desk, its corner is already torn, and Xu Lan has not yet walked to the window.” If the style sample contains another person wearing a raincoat, do not bring them into the weather station just because you are referencing its style. The bright background on the character sheet must not override the night-shift room’s lighting.

heading.zh: 多张参考互相打架时怎样修
heading.en: How to Resolve Conflicts Between References

body.zh:
| 冲突 | 原因 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 角色脸稳定，但服装一直回到旧版 | 身份参考越权控制临时造型 | 把当前造型单独绑定，并明确身份参考不控制换装 |
| 场景入口总换边 | 构图图与地理图职责混在一起 | 地理参考优先固定入口；构图只控制当前取景布局 |
| 风格图带来陌生文字或人物 | “风格”被当成整图复刻 | 限定到色彩、材质等视觉语言，保护身份、文字和人数 |
| 首帧已经出现动作结果 | 起始帧参考越过镜头过程 | 恢复起点；终点需要时单列结束帧，且必须来自既定镜头 |
| 声称已检查水印但无人看过图 | 观察状态不真实 | 标未验证，获得授权观察后再记录实际可见内容 |
body.en:
| Conflict | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The character’s face stays consistent, but the outfit keeps reverting to an old version | The identity reference is over-controlling temporary appearance | Bind the current appearance state separately and state that identity references do not control wardrobe changes |
| The entrance keeps switching sides | Composition and geography are mixed together | Let the geography reference fix the entrance; let composition control only the current framing |
| The style image introduces unfamiliar text or people | “Style” is being treated as a full-image copy | Limit it to visual language such as color and material; protect identity, text and subject count |
