If the segment merely repeats the same joke in a new location, shorten it. The next segment should carry forward a promise, question, or responsibility left by the last one. The ending may restore the original bodies or leave the swap in place, but the characters must address the relationship consequences already created. Returning to their bodies does not automatically revoke promises made while standing in for one another.

q.zh: 必须一直瞒着所有配角吗？
q.en: Must the swap stay secret from every supporting character?

a.zh: 可以让部分人先知情，他们因此成为帮手、核验者或新的压力来源。保密只是人物策略；当披露能更好推动选择和后果时，让人物承担披露的代价，不必无限重复险些露馅。
a.en: No. Some people can learn the truth earlier and become helpers, verifiers, or new sources of pressure. Secrecy is only a character strategy. When disclosure better advances choice and consequence, let the characters pay its cost rather than repeating near-exposures forever.

q.zh: 身体互换和冒名顶替能用同一方法吗？
q.en: Can body-swap and impersonation stories use the same method?

a.zh: 都能用任务、身份权限、识别依据和误认后果检查剧情，但来源不同。身体互换先定意识与身体规则；冒名顶替则要交代伪装为什么暂时成立、哪些核验会使它失效。不要用互换设定替冒名者省掉伪装过程。
a.en: Both can be checked through tasks, identity permissions, recognition evidence, and consequences of misidentification, but their premises differ. A body-swap story first defines how consciousness and body work. An impersonation story must establish why the disguise holds temporarily and which checks would break it. Do not use a swap premise to skip the work of disguise for an impostor.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-develop（Codex 中用 $short-drama-develop），根据我的互换设定规划故事引擎：外部任务、身份限制、各人已知与误信、逐段任务结果和关系后果。先保留已定互换规则，不写单集正文。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-develop` to plan the story engine from my body-swap premise: the external task, identity constraints, what each person knows or mistakenly believes, and the task result and relationship consequence of each segment. Preserve the established swap rules and do not write episode scripts yet. In Codex, use `$short-drama-develop`.

title.zh: 视频剪辑节奏怎么把控：删等待，留下动作和反应
title.en: How to Control Editing Rhythm: Cut Waiting, Keep Action and Reaction

seo_title.zh: 视频剪辑节奏怎么把控｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Control Video Editing Rhythm | ZenStory

description.zh: 从具体入点、出点和反应镜头判断节奏，区分无效等待与必要停顿，附原创剪点对照和接点复看方法。
description.en: Judge rhythm through precise in and out points and reaction shots. Separate dead time from useful pauses with an original cut comparison and review method.

answer.zh: 剪辑节奏先看观众理解与感受是否完成，再看镜头长短。压缩已经能推断的准备过程，保留使选择成立的前提、动作完成和关键反应。画面太碎时先检查哪些切点新增了信息，哪些只是打断；移动入出点或恢复原镜连续，往往比再加转场更直接。
answer.en: Editing rhythm begins with whether the viewer has finished understanding and feeling a beat, not with shot length. Compress setup the viewer can already infer, while preserving the premise that makes a choice intelligible, the completion of an action, and the crucial reaction. If the footage feels choppy, first ask which cuts add information and which merely interrupt. Moving an in or out point, or restoring a continuous source shot, is often more direct than adding another transition.

heading.zh: 每一剪之前，先指出发生了什么变化
heading.en: Before Every Cut, Name What Has Changed

body.zh:
把“这里有一件大事”具体到一个能看见或听见的时刻：谁得知消息、改变决定、失去优势，或作出回应。随后确定这一下落在说话者、听者、动作还是物件上。

一个事件可以跨几个镜头；一个镜头也可以容纳多次变化。不要把整段平均切成一样长，也不要以切点越多证明节奏越快。先确认去掉这一段会失去哪项理解，再决定能压缩多少。
body.en:
Make “something important happens here” specific enough to see or hear: someone learns news, changes a decision, loses an advantage, or responds. Then decide whether that beat belongs on the speaker, listener, action, or object.

One event may span several shots, and one shot may contain several changes. Do not divide an entire passage into equal lengths, and do not treat more cuts as proof of faster pacing. First identify what understanding would be lost if a passage were removed; only then decide how much to compress.

heading.zh: 入点和出点分别承担什么
heading.en: What In Points and Out Points Each Need to Do

body.zh:
| 检查位置 | 可以尝试压缩 | 需要保住 |
|---|---|---|
| 入点之前 | 已经能推断的走路、等候、重复交代 | 人物为何作出下一动作的必要前提 |
| 动作之中 | 没有新变化的机械重复 | 转手、停下、拒绝等可辨认的完成状态 |
| 台词之后 | 信息已经落地的空等 | 听者理解、犹豫或改变选择的反应 |
| 场景之间 | 没有作用的过场 | 新地点建立、声音接力或有意并置的边界 |

晚进入之前问“观众还知道他为什么这样做吗”；早离开之前问“观众看见后果了吗”。保留多少需要回到具体表演，不用统一秒数代替判断。
body.en:
| Point to inspect | You can try compressing | You need to preserve |
|---|---|---|
| Before the in point | Walking, waiting, or repeated setup the viewer can already infer | The premise needed to understand why the character takes the next action |
| During the action | Mechanical repetition with no new change | A recognizable completion state, such as a handoff, stop, or refusal |
| After dialogue | Empty waiting after the information has landed | The listener’s understanding, hesitation, or changed choice |
| Between scenes | Transitional material with no function | Establishment of a new location, a sound bridge, or an intentional juxtaposition |

Before entering later, ask, “Will the viewer still know why this person acts?” Before leaving earlier, ask, “Has the viewer seen the consequence?” Return to the specific performance to decide how much to retain; do not replace judgment with a universal number of seconds.

heading.zh: 原创剪点对照：维修摊前的一张旧合照
heading.en: Original Cut Comparison: An Old Photo at a Repair Stall

body.zh:
以下是为说明剪辑方法设计的虚构素材，不是已经拍摄或试听过的视频。素材中，老人拿来损坏的相框，说只想把玻璃换好，旧照片不要动。修理者先答应，拆开背板后发现照片后面写着一句给家人的留言。他看向老人，老人伸手压住背板，停了一下，才说：“别给他们看。”修理者把背板翻回去，取来不透明的衬纸。

| 版本 | 剪点处理 | 观众可能失去什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 过度压缩 | 从拆背板直接跳到放衬纸 | 看不见留言、目光和保密请求，衬纸像无缘无故的操作 |
| 只留说话者 | 保留老人的要求，删去修理者停手、翻回背板 | 听见请求，却看不见对方是否接受 |
| 保留因果与回应 | 缩短找工具过程，保留留言露出、老人压住背板、保密请求与翻回动作 | 观众能理解修理者改变处理方式的原因 |

“别给他们看”之后的停留要容得下接受请求的动作。若原素材只有沉默而没有能辨认的回应，应重新挑选真实存在的时刻，或保留原有不确定性，不能另拼一段点头冒充承诺。
body.en:
The following fictional footage was designed to illustrate editing choices. This is not footage that has actually been filmed or reviewed. An older man brings in a damaged picture frame and says he wants only the glass replaced; the old photograph must remain untouched. The repairer agrees. After removing the backing, he finds a message to the family written behind the photo. He looks toward the customer. The older man reaches out, presses down the backing, pauses, and says, “Don’t show them.” The repairer turns the backing over again and fetches an opaque liner.

| Version | Cut treatment | What the viewer may lose |
|---|---|---|
| Over-compressed | Jumps directly from removing the backing to inserting the liner | The message, exchanged glance, and request for secrecy disappear, so the liner seems arbitrary |
| Keeps only the speaker | Preserves the older man’s request but removes the repairer stopping and turning the backing over | The viewer hears the request but cannot see whether it was accepted |
| Preserves cause and response | Shortens the search for tools but keeps the revealed message, the hand on the backing, the request, and the action of turning it back over | The viewer understands why the repairer changes his method |

After “Don’t show them,” the shot must last long enough for the accepting action to occur. If the source contains only silence and no recognizable response, choose another moment that genuinely exists or preserve the original uncertainty. Do not splice in an unrelated nod and present it as a promise.

heading.zh: 觉得太碎，先分清切点是谁造成的
heading.en: If It Feels Choppy, Identify What Created Each Cut

body.zh:
- **原片本来就在切**：保留承担信息的完整镜头；想延长反应时，多保留真实存在的源素材，而非默认定格出一段新表演。
- **本次截取造成跳动**：把边界移到完整动作、句尾或自然停顿；相邻片段本就连续时，可以恢复连续播放。
- **有意的快切段落**：正常速度观看，判断每个短镜头是否提供新信息、节奏或动作结果。有效的短镜头不应只因短就被删。

不要用闪白或溶解盖住未解决的因果跳跃，也不要在原片叠化中途再截一刀。声音边界与画面边界冲突时，先保证关键台词完整，再调整画面选择。
body.en:
- **The source itself already cuts:** Preserve complete shots that carry information. To lengthen a reaction, retain more source footage that actually exists rather than automatically freezing a frame to invent a new performance.
- **Your excerpt created the jump:** Move the boundary to a completed action, sentence ending, or natural pause. If adjacent excerpts were continuous in the source, restore continuous playback.
- **The rapid cutting is intentional:** Watch at normal speed and ask whether each brief shot supplies new information, rhythm, or an action result. A useful short shot should not be deleted merely for being short.

Do not use a flash or dissolve to conceal an unresolved causal jump, and do not cut again in the middle of a dissolve already present in the source. When sound and picture boundaries conflict, preserve the complete crucial line first and then adjust the visual selection.

heading.zh: 最终检查要回到真实播放
heading.en: Final Review Must Return to Real-Time Playback

body.zh:
局部来回看接点，再按正常速度完整看这一段。检查台词有没有被截断，空间是否突然难以辨认，动作是否完成两次，反应有没有落地。镜头检测或接点截图只能帮你找到可疑位置，不能证明正常播放舒服。

把这次要改的切点写具体：原段保留什么、新入点或出点为什么更好、哪些声音和结果不能丢。先处理影响理解最大的几处，别为了全片显得“统一”把每段都改成同一速度。
body.en:
Review the join repeatedly in context, then watch the entire passage once at normal speed. Check whether dialogue is clipped, space suddenly becomes hard to understand, an action completes twice, or a reaction never lands. Shot detection and cut-point screenshots can identify suspicious places; they cannot prove that normal playback feels right.

Describe each proposed change precisely: what remains from the source, why the new in or out point is better, and which sound or result must not be lost. Fix the few cuts that most damage understanding first. Do not force every passage to the same speed merely to make the whole video look “consistent.”

q.zh: 反应镜头是不是容易拖慢节奏？
q.en: Do reaction shots always slow the pace?

a.zh: 反应带来关系变化、知情变化或新决定时，它就是内容。重复已经明确的情绪可以压缩；第一次让观众看懂选择后果的反应值得留下。
a.en: A reaction is content when it changes a relationship, who knows what, or a decision. A repeated emotion already made clear can be compressed; the first reaction that lets viewers understand the consequence of a choice is worth keeping.

q.zh: 能把不同场景拼成一个动作吗？
q.en: Can I combine actions from different scenes into one?

a.zh: 可以明确做对比或主题并置，但不能把原本无关的出手、接触和反应拼成同场真实因果。剪辑后产生的新含义必须能被素材支持，字幕也不能替不存在的证据兜底。
a.en: You can create a clearly framed comparison or thematic juxtaposition, but you cannot combine unrelated gestures, contact, and reactions into a false same-scene cause and effect. The new meaning created by an edit must be supported by the footage, and captions cannot substitute for evidence that does not exist.

text.zh: 使用 /video-recap（Codex 中用 $video-recap）处理我提供的本地视频时，说明要剪成原声短片或解说片，并指出需保留的台词、动作与反应。它会进入视频理解和制作流程；如只需讨论剪点，先明确本轮只给修改建议，不运行剪辑、配音或合成。
text.en: When using `/video-recap` to process a local video I provide, I will specify whether I want an original-audio short or a narrated recap and identify dialogue, actions, and reactions that must remain. This starts the video-understanding and production workflow. If I only want to discuss cut points, I will state that this round should provide revision advice only, without editing, voice-over, or rendering. In Codex, use `$video-recap`.

title.zh: 小说转场怎么写：让前一场把读者送进下一场
title.en: How to Write Scene Transitions: Let One Scene Lead into the Next

seo_title.zh: 小说转场怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Scene Transitions in Fiction | ZenStory

description.zh: 小说场景切换不必交代全部路程。判断何时跳切，再用未完成的因果、问题、情绪余波或物件声音承接下一场。附原创气象站案例。
description.en: Decide when to jump ahead, then bridge scenes through causality, questions, emotional residue, objects, or sound. Includes a weather-station example.

answer.zh: 自然转场要让前一场留下能跨过切口的东西：下一步行动、待回答的问题、尚未消化的情绪，或会在新地点继续出现的物件与声音。一句“与此同时”和完整赶路都不是必需。没有新信息的过程可以直接跳过；新场开头要尽快说明谁、在哪里、正在处理什么，并让承接项发生变化。
answer.en: A natural transition carries something across the cut: the next action, an unanswered question, an unprocessed emotion, or an object or sound that continues in the new place. Neither “meanwhile” nor a complete travel sequence is required. Skip processes that add no new information. At the start of the new scene, quickly establish who is present, where they are, and what they are handling, then change the element carried across.

heading.zh: 先判断：这一段需要写，还是应该跳过
heading.en: First Decide: Does This Passage Need a Scene, or Should You Skip It?

body.zh:
场景结束后，列出人物抵达下一场之前可能发生的步骤。只有会改变信息、关系、风险、资源或选择的步骤才值得成场；买票、乘车、开门若只是完成移动，可以一句带过或直接切到结果。

转场不是独立的填充段。它至少完成一项工作：兑现上一场的后果、提出下一步目标、保存一股情绪压力，或把读者注意力交给另一条线。删掉切口附近的句子再读，若人物为何来到新场仍然清楚，就不必把路程补回来。
body.en:
After a scene ends, list the steps that might occur before the character reaches the next one. Only a step that changes information, relationships, risk, resources, or choices deserves a scene. Buying a ticket, riding a train, or opening a door can be summarized in one line or skipped if it only completes movement.

A transition is not an independent filler passage. It must do at least one job: deliver the consequence of the last scene, establish the next goal, preserve emotional pressure, or hand the reader’s attention to another plotline. Remove the sentences around the cut and reread. If it remains clear why the character has arrived in the new scene, you do not need to restore the journey.

heading.zh: 四种可跨场的承接物
heading.en: Four Things That Can Bridge Scenes

body.zh:
| 承接方式 | 前一场留下什么 | 新一场怎样接 |
|---|---|---|
| 因果 | 一个决定、命令或损失 | 直接写它造成的下一步行动 |
| 问题 | 一个具体未解疑问 | 用调查、误判或局部答案推进 |
| 情绪余波 | 人物尚未处理的羞愧、兴奋或戒备 | 让它改变新场中的说法与选择 |
| 物件或声音 | 信件、污迹、铃声、广播等具体对象 | 在新时空获得新用途或含义 |

同一处选最有力的一条即可。相似物、光影或声音可以让画面顺滑，但若新场没有推进，它只是漂亮的连接。反过来，只要因果清楚，干净的空行也可以完成跳切。
body.en:
| Bridge | What the first scene leaves behind | How the new scene picks it up |
|---|---|---|
| Causality | A decision, order, or loss | Show the next action it directly causes |
| Question | One specific unresolved question | Advance it through investigation, misjudgment, or a partial answer |
| Emotional residue | Shame, excitement, or wariness the character has not processed | Let it alter what the character says and chooses in the new scene |
| Object or sound | A concrete item such as a letter, stain, bell, or broadcast | Give it a new use or meaning in the new time and place |

Choose the strongest one at a given cut. Similar objects, light, or sound can smooth the image, but the link is merely attractive if the new scene does not advance. Conversely, when causality is clear, a clean section break can complete the jump.

heading.zh: 新场开头先给定位，再制造变化
heading.en: Orient the Reader at the New Scene, Then Create Change

body.zh:
新场第一小段回答读者此刻真正需要的三件事：视角人物是谁、地点或时间发生了什么变化、他正处理上一场留下的哪件事。不要把日期、天气、房间陈设和人物履历一次性重报。

承接不等于复述。上一场以“她决定去查停机记录”结束，新场无需再写“她想着一定要查清”。让她已经站在档案柜前，却发现记录页被替换，读者会从行动认出承接，同时收到新变化。多线切换时，每条线切出前留下可继续的问题；切回来时先推进这个问题，避免重新介绍人物。
body.en:
The first short passage of a new scene should answer the three things readers actually need now: whose viewpoint this is, what has changed in time or place, and which matter from the prior scene the character is addressing. Do not report the date, weather, room furnishings, and character history all over again.

A bridge is not a recap. If the prior scene ends with “She decided to inspect the shutdown records,” the new scene need not repeat that she was determined to investigate. Put her at the archive cabinet, where she discovers that a record page has been replaced. Readers recognize the continuation through action and receive a new change at the same time. When alternating plotlines, leave each line with a question that can continue. When returning, advance that question before reintroducing anyone.

heading.zh: 原创范例：山顶气象站的两次切换
heading.en: Original Example: Two Transitions at a Mountaintop Weather Station

body.zh:
实习观测员简遥发现山谷的自动雨量记录比手写值少了一截。值班长让她先别上报，声称传感器结露很常见。她在记录纸背面看见一道圆形水印，决定去旧设备库找同批纸卷。

**拖沓版**会写她收好本子、穿外套、下楼、沿走廊走到库房，再详细描写开锁。动作完整，却没有变化。

**因果跳切**可以直接写：

> 旧设备库只剩一个空纸箱。简遥把记录纸扣在箱底，圆形水印正好压住一圈褪色的罐底印。箱底旁边还粘着半张防潮剂标签，型号一栏依然清楚。

地点已经改变，“去找纸卷”的决定得到结果，箱底痕迹和残留标签提供了进一步调查的线索，尚未证明谁更换过记录。

她把罐底印与标签一起拍下，库房所在山谷没有手机信号。下一场切到翌日镇上的维修铺：

> 卷帘门刚抬到一半，店里的气压警报器先响了。老板看清她照片里的型号标签，伸手关掉警报：“这个型号，我店里三年前就不进货了，旧单据还在。”

从山谷赶到镇上的路程不必展开；维修铺的警报快速建立新场景，照片承接调查目标，这条证词把下一步引向旧进货单据。停止进货的时间还不能直接证明记录何时被更换。
body.en:
Junior observer Jian Yao discovers that the valley’s automated rainfall record is substantially lower than the handwritten figure. The shift supervisor tells her not to report it yet, claiming sensor condensation is common. On the back of the record sheet she notices a circular water mark and decides to search the old equipment store for paper rolls from the same batch.

A **dragging version** would show her putting away her notebook, putting on a coat, going downstairs, walking along the corridor, and then unlocking the storeroom in detail. The movements are complete, but nothing changes.

A **causal jump** can begin here:

> Only an empty carton remained in the old equipment store. Jian Yao laid the record sheet against the bottom. Its circular water mark fit a faded ring left by a can. Beside the ring, half a desiccant label was still stuck to the cardboard, and the model number remained legible.

The location has changed and the decision to find the paper rolls has produced a result. The mark and partial label provide leads for further investigation without proving who replaced the record.

She photographs the ring and label, but the valley containing the storeroom has no cell service. The next scene cuts to a repair shop in town the following day:

> The pressure alarm inside sounded before the rolling shutter was halfway up. The owner recognized the model number in her photograph and reached over to silence the alarm. “I stopped stocking this model three years ago. I still have the old invoices.”

The trip from the valley to town need not be shown. The alarm quickly establishes the repair shop, the photograph carries the investigative goal forward, and the testimony points toward old purchase records. The date when the shop stopped stocking the model still does not directly prove when the record was replaced.

heading.zh: 转场生硬或拖沓时怎么改
heading.en: How to Repair Abrupt or Dragging Transitions

body.zh:
| 症状 | 原因 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|
| 每次都写人物离开、赶路、抵达 | 把空间连续误当成叙事连续 | 跳到下一次有变化的动作 |
| 用“与此同时”切到无关人物 | 两条线没有共同问题 | 先让切出线留下会被另一线影响的信息 |
| 新场开头复述上一场结论 | 只承接，没有推进 | 从结论造成的阻碍、发现或选择写起 |
| 用相似物硬转，逻辑却断了 | 视觉相似代替了因果 | 补清谁为何来到这里、要处理什么 |
| 高压场后立刻完全松弛 | 情绪结果被清零 | 让余波改变新场的节奏或人物策略 |
| 频繁切线却迟迟不回来 | 每条线只留钩子不交付 | 切回时先回答一部分，再提出新问题 |
body.en:
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every scene shows the character leaving, traveling, and arriving | Spatial continuity is mistaken for narrative continuity | Jump to the next action that changes something |
| “Meanwhile” cuts to an unrelated character | The two lines share no question | Before cutting away, leave information that the other line can affect |
| A new scene opens by repeating the last scene’s conclusion | The transition continues but does not advance | Begin with the obstacle, discovery, or choice caused by that conclusion |
| A similar image forces a transition while the logic breaks | Visual resemblance has replaced causality | Clarify who came here, why, and what they need to handle |
| A high-pressure scene is followed by complete relaxation | The emotional consequence has been reset | Let the residue alter the new scene’s rhythm or strategy |
| The narrative switches lines repeatedly and takes too long to return | Every line leaves hooks but delivers nothing | On returning, answer something before raising a new question |

q.zh: 转场一定要写过渡句吗？
q.en: Does every scene transition need a transitional sentence?

a.zh: 不需要。因果清楚时，分段、空行或新章节就能完成转场。过渡句只在时间、地点或人物关系容易误读时补足必要定位。
a.en: No. When causality is clear, a section break, blank line, or new chapter can complete the transition. Add a transitional sentence only when time, location, or relationships would otherwise be misread.

q.zh: 同一章可以切换很多场景吗？
q.en: Can one chapter contain many scene changes?

a.zh: 可以，但每次切换都应让故事获得新信息、行动或对照，并让读者迅速定位。若几个短场只重复同一结论，可以合并或保留最有变化的一场。
a.en: Yes, but each switch should add information, action, or contrast and let readers reorient quickly. If several brief scenes repeat the same conclusion, combine them or keep the one that changes the most.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 检查这几处场景转场，逐处判断哪些过程应跳过，并标出跨场的因果、问题、情绪余波或物件声音；让新场开头快速定位并推进，不改既有剧情事实”（Codex 中使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to inspect these scene transitions. At each one, decide which process should be skipped and identify the causality, question, emotional residue, object, or sound that crosses the cut. Orient the reader quickly at each new scene and move it forward without changing established plot facts.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说回忆怎么写：让过去改变眼前的选择
title.en: How to Write Flashbacks: Make the Past Change a Present Choice

seo_title.zh: 小说回忆与插叙怎么写不打断剧情｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Flashbacks Without Stalling | ZenStory

description.zh: 回忆和插叙要由当前场景触发，只带回会改变判断、关系或选择的过去事实，并在返回当下后产生动作。附原创修琴案例。
description.en: Trigger a flashback from the present, retrieve only what changes judgment, relationships, or choice, then act on it. Includes a repair-shop example.

answer.zh: 写回忆前先确定它要改变当下什么。由眼前可感知的物件、声音、话语或处境触发，只进入当前决定所需的过去片段；一旦关键差异出现，就回到现在，让人物据此改口、行动、拒绝或付出代价。若回忆只是复述读者已知内容，或删掉后当前选择不变，就应压缩或删除。
answer.en: Before writing a flashback, decide what it will change in the present. Trigger it through a current object, sound, remark, or situation, and enter only the part of the past needed for the present decision. Once the crucial difference appears, return to the present and let the character change what they say or do, what they refuse, or what cost they pay as a result. If a flashback repeats what readers already know, or removing it leaves the present choice unchanged, compress or delete it.

heading.zh: 先写回忆带回来的新作用
heading.en: First Define the New Function the Flashback Brings Back

body.zh:
回忆不是补人物档案的容器。落笔前填一句：人物想起这件事以后，眼前的判断、关系或选择从什么变成什么。

| 回忆带回什么 | 当下应出现的变化 |
|---|---|
| 被忽略的事实 | 改变怀疑对象或行动方向 |
| 旧承诺的真实含义 | 接受、拒绝或重新谈条件 |
| 某人的一贯做法 | 预判对方下一步并采取措施 |
| 一段关系中的误读 | 改变说法、距离或愿意承担的代价 |

只为了证明人物“有过去”，可以把必要背景压成一句；只有过去内部存在需要亲历的转折，才值得展开成较完整片段。
body.en:
A flashback is not a container for a character dossier. Before drafting, complete this sentence: After remembering this, the character’s present judgment, relationship, or choice changes from what to what?

| What the flashback retrieves | Change that should appear in the present |
|---|---|
| An overlooked fact | Change the suspect or direction of action |
| The true meaning of an old promise | Accept, refuse, or renegotiate terms |
| Someone’s habitual method | Anticipate the person’s next move and take action |
| A misreading within a relationship | Change the wording, distance, or cost the character will bear |

If the only purpose is to prove that the character “has a past,” compress the necessary background into a sentence. A more complete scene is worthwhile only when the past itself contains a turn the reader needs to experience.

heading.zh: 用当前触发进入，用当前动作退出
heading.en: Enter Through a Present Trigger and Exit Through Present Action

body.zh:
有效回忆有三个连接点：

1. **当前触发**：气味、声音、物件、动作或一句话碰到旧经验。
2. **关键差异**：过去片段提供此前没有或此前理解错的信息。
3. **现在回收**：触发物仍在场，人物用新理解完成一个动作。

触发不必写成“她陷入回忆”。让人物摸到琴箱裂口，过去那次修补便可以进入；回忆结束时，她仍握着裂口，并据此决定是否交琴。首尾共享一个具体对象，读者更容易辨认时空。
body.en:
An effective flashback has three connection points:

1. **Present trigger:** A smell, sound, object, action, or remark touches an old experience.
2. **Crucial difference:** The past supplies information that was previously unknown or misunderstood.
3. **Present action:** The trigger remains in the scene, and the character uses the new understanding to complete an action.

The trigger need not be announced as “She fell into a memory.” A character touches a crack in an instrument case, and the old repair can enter. When the flashback ends, she is still holding the crack and decides from it whether to surrender the instrument. Sharing a concrete object at the entrance and exit helps readers track time.

heading.zh: 回忆写到哪里停：以当前问题为边界
heading.en: Where to End a Flashback: Let the Present Question Set the Boundary

body.zh:
从当前决定倒推所需信息，出现后就停。人物此刻只需确认父亲是否动过琴，不必顺便交代童年、搬家和求学经历。长度由功能决定，不设统一句数。

若过去片段本身包含新的冲突与结果，可以展开；若只是资料，概述通常更清楚。插入较长回忆前，先让当前场景形成明确压力，返回后立即处理这股压力。这样读者知道为什么此刻要看过去，也能看到它不是暂停键。
body.en:
Work backward from the present decision to identify the needed information, and stop once it appears. If the character only needs to establish whether her father touched the instrument, there is no need to add her childhood, family move, and education. Function determines length; there is no universal sentence count.

If the past scene contains its own conflict and result, it may expand. If it is merely data, a summary is usually clearer. Before inserting a long flashback, establish clear pressure in the present scene, then address that pressure immediately on returning. Readers understand why they are seeing the past now and can see that it is not a pause button.

heading.zh: 原创范例：琴箱里少了一枚铜扣
heading.en: Original Example: A Missing Brass Clasp in the Instrument Case

body.zh:
古琴修复师许潭筠准备把师父留下的琴交给博物馆。验收员指出琴箱右侧缺了一枚铜扣，怀疑运输中损坏。许潭筠本想签下责任单，手指却摸到扣眼内侧一层旧蜡。

过去的片段由“旧蜡”触发：十二岁那年停电，师父在烛下拆掉这枚铜扣，把它压在摇晃的工作台脚下。许潭筠问为何不换块木片，师父说这张桌子明早要修一把被火烤裂的琴，今晚不能再晃。后来铜扣没有装回去，她一直以为师父粗心。

回忆停在这个差异上，不继续讲她怎样学琴、怎样继承铺子。回到验收室，她没有签运输损坏，而是请对方先检查旧蜡年代，并把工作台也列入捐赠清单。过去改变了责任判断，也让一件原本不起眼的工具进入眼前行动。

若前文已经完整写过停电修琴，再原样回放就没有新作用。可以压成：“扣眼里的蜡还在——师父曾拿它垫过那张工作台。”随后直接写她撤回责任单。
body.en:
Guqin conservator Xu Tanyun is preparing to donate the instrument left by her mentor to a museum. The receiving officer points out that a brass clasp is missing from the right side of the case and suspects damage in transit. Xu Tanyun is about to sign the liability form when her finger touches a layer of old wax inside the clasp hole.

The **old wax** triggers the past. During a blackout when she was twelve, her mentor removed the clasp by candlelight and wedged it under a wobbling workbench leg. Xu Tanyun asked why he did not use a scrap of wood. He said he needed the table steady to repair a fire-cracked instrument the next morning, so it could not wobble that night. The clasp was never reattached, and she had always assumed her mentor was careless.

The flashback stops at that difference instead of continuing through how she learned the instrument or inherited the shop. Back in the receiving room, she refuses to sign for transit damage. She asks the officer to date the old wax first and add the workbench to the donation list. The past changes the judgment of responsibility and brings an overlooked tool into present action.

If the blackout repair has already appeared in full earlier, replaying it unchanged adds nothing. Compress it to: “The wax was still inside the clasp hole—her mentor had once used the clasp to steady that workbench.” Then move directly to her withdrawing the liability form.

heading.zh: 回忆打断剧情的常见原因
heading.en: Why Flashbacks Commonly Interrupt the Plot

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 角色一见物件就回顾完整人生 | 只取当前选择所需的一个差异 |
| 回忆重复读者刚看过的事件 | 增加新的视角或压成一句承接 |
| 过去很动人，回来后一切照旧 | 让它改变判断、话术、行动或代价 |
| 回忆中继续套回忆 | 选一个明确时段，其他信息概述 |
| 用大段前史解释世界规则 | 把当前规则放回行动后果，回忆只留人物经验 |
| 回到现在没有定位 | 重现触发物、未完动作或正在等待的对方 |

修订时把“进入前的当前问题”和“返回后的新动作”并排看。二者没有因果，说明这段过去尚未接上现在。
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| A character sees an object and reviews an entire life | Take only the one difference needed for the present choice |
| The flashback repeats an event readers just witnessed | Add a new viewpoint or compress it to one bridging sentence |
| The past is moving, but nothing changes after the return | Let it change judgment, language, action, or cost |
| One flashback nests another | Choose one clear period and summarize the rest |
| A long backstory explains all the world’s rules | Put current rules back into the consequences of action; keep only lived experience in the memory |
| The return to the present has no orientation | Reintroduce the trigger, unfinished action, or waiting person |

During revision, place the present question before the flashback beside the new action after it. If they have no causal connection, the past has not yet joined the present.

q.zh: 回忆可以放在小说开头吗？
q.en: Can a novel open with a flashback?

a.zh: 可以，但读者仍需要知道是谁在何种当前压力下想起它。若开头整段只有过去，先判断直接从过去时段开场是否更清楚，不必把正常叙事硬标成回忆。
a.en: Yes, but readers still need to know who remembers it and under what present pressure. If the opening consists entirely of the past, ask whether beginning directly in that period would be clearer instead of labeling ordinary narration as a flashback.

q.zh: 怎样区分回忆和设定介绍？
q.en: How is a flashback different from worldbuilding exposition?

a.zh: 回忆是某个人经历过、并会影响其当前理解的过去；设定介绍说明世界如何运作。两者可以相遇，但不要借人物想起往事一次讲完所有规则。
a.en: A flashback is a past event someone experienced that changes their present understanding. Worldbuilding exposition explains how the world works. They can overlap, but do not use a character’s memory to deliver every rule at once.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 检查这段回忆或插叙，写清当前触发、过去带回的新差异和返回当下后的行动；删去不改变判断与选择的前史，不新增人物经历”（Codex 中使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to inspect this flashback. Identify the present trigger, the new difference retrieved from the past, and the action taken after returning to the present. Remove backstory that does not change judgment or choice, and add no new character history.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说环境描写怎么写：让人物在场景里行动
title.en: How to Write Setting Description: Let Characters Act in the Scene

seo_title.zh: 小说环境描写怎么写才不水｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Writing Setting Description Without Padding | ZenStory

description.zh: 环境描写不靠景物清单，而要选择人物此刻会注意、会碰到、会因此改变行动的细节。附原创停电温室案例与删改方法。
description.en: Choose setting details a character would notice, touch, and act on instead of listing scenery. Includes a greenhouse blackout and revision method.

answer.zh: 先写人物进入场景要做什么，再选择会帮助、阻碍、误导或逼迫他的环境细节。描写落到主动注意、身体或工具与环境的交互，以及交互造成的判断和行动后果。气氛可以保留，但要通过具体感受影响阅读节奏；若删掉一段景物后人物处境、信息和体验都不变，就应压缩。
answer.en: Start with what the character must accomplish in the scene, then choose environmental details that help, obstruct, mislead, or pressure them. Description becomes part of the scene when it shows active attention, the body or a tool interacting with the surroundings, and the consequences for judgment and action. Atmosphere still matters, but it should shape reading rhythm through concrete sensation. If removing a passage leaves the character’s situation, information, and experience unchanged, compress it.

heading.zh: 按人物目标筛选环境信息
heading.en: Filter Setting Details Through the Character’s Goal

body.zh:
同一间仓库，失火后来找出口的人会注意风向、烟层与门把温度；来盘点货物的人会看标签、受潮痕迹与堆放顺序。环境细节由目标、经验和风险筛选，因而也能表现人物。

动笔前回答：人物来这里要完成什么？哪项环境条件会改变完成方式？他凭什么注意到这项条件？这样写出的景物属于当前场景，从而避免写成可搬到任何章节的装饰。
body.en:
In the same warehouse, a person searching for an exit after a fire notices wind direction, the smoke layer, and the temperature of a door handle. Someone taking inventory notices labels, damp marks, and stacking order. Goals, experience, and risk filter environmental details, so those details can also reveal character.

Before drafting, ask: What must the character accomplish here? Which environmental condition changes how it can be done? What qualifies the character to notice that condition? The resulting description belongs to this scene rather than serving as decoration that could be moved into any chapter.

heading.zh: 把景物写进“注意—交互—后果”
heading.en: Build Description as Attention, Interaction, and Consequence

body.zh:
| 环节 | 要写什么 | 避免什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 注意 | 人物因目标或经验捕捉到的异常 | 从天花板到地板逐项扫描 |
| 交互 | 触碰、绕开、借用、试探或被环境限制 | 人物站着欣赏，景物自行表演 |
| 后果 | 信息、行动、关系或身体状态改变 | 描写完立即忘记场景条件 |

五感不是配额。能决定动作的湿滑触感，比同时补齐颜色、气味、声音更有用。动态变化尤其有效：光线熄灭、风把门推回、地面积水上涨，都能迫使人物重新选择。
body.en:
| Stage | What to write | What to avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Attention | An anomaly the character catches because of a goal or experience | Scanning item by item from ceiling to floor |
| Interaction | Touching, avoiding, using, testing, or being constrained by the environment | A character standing still to admire scenery while the setting performs by itself |
| Consequence | A change in information, action, relationships, or physical state | Forgetting the conditions immediately after describing them |

The five senses are not a quota. A slippery surface that determines an action is more useful than filling in color, smell, and sound at once. Dynamic changes are especially effective: the lights go out, wind pushes a door closed, or rising water forces the character to choose again.

heading.zh: 写气氛时，让场景产生压力而非替人物下结论
heading.en: For Atmosphere, Let the Setting Apply Pressure Instead of Declaring Emotion

body.zh:
“夜色压抑”“房间温馨”先给结论，读者却不知道这股气氛怎样发生。可以选择一两个会持续影响现场的条件：过亮的走廊让人无处躲藏；持续滴水让谈话一次次被打断；拥挤的桌椅迫使两人无法保持距离。

环境可以呼应情绪，也可以反衬。人物收到坏消息时窗外不必下雨；晴天里照常进行的庆典，反而可能加重他的孤立。关键是人物如何使用、抵抗或误读这个环境，天气无需替他感受。
body.en:
“The night felt oppressive” and “the room was cozy” announce conclusions without showing how the atmosphere occurs. Instead, choose one or two conditions that keep affecting the scene: an overlit corridor leaves nowhere to hide; steady dripping repeatedly interrupts a conversation; crowded furniture prevents two people from keeping their distance.

The setting may echo emotion or work against it. Bad news does not require rain outside. A celebration proceeding under bright skies can deepen a character’s isolation. What matters is how the character uses, resists, or misreads the setting. The weather need not feel on the character’s behalf.

heading.zh: 原创范例：停电后的社区温室
heading.en: Original Example: A Community Greenhouse After a Blackout

body.zh:
志愿者高槐音夜里赶到社区温室，要在降温前转移一批幼苗。若只写“温室里潮湿发冷，玻璃上全是水雾，四周很黑”，气氛有了，行动仍未发生。

改写时让环境参与选择：

> 应急灯只照亮门边两排架子。高槐音伸手去搬育苗盘，塑料边缘却粘在铁架上——白天漏出的营养液已经冻住。她没再硬扯，先摘下围巾裹住最靠风口的一盘，又把浇水软管拖到门缝下。水管里的余水结成一节节硬骨，门因此关不严。
>
> 她顺着水管往里摸，发现阀门还在滴。若先救幼苗，冷风会继续灌进来；若去关总阀，门边这几盘要留在原地。她把应急灯放到地上，对刚赶来的邻居说：“你抱盘，我去找阀。别拔，先拧松架子上的冰。”

灯光范围、结冰的营养液、风口和水管都改变任务；高槐音如何注意并处理它们，也体现她熟悉温室。没有必要再补一段植物香气，除非气味将提供泄漏或腐坏的信息。
body.en:
Volunteer Gao Huaiyin arrives at a community greenhouse at night to move a batch of seedlings before the temperature drops. Simply writing, “The greenhouse was damp and cold, mist covered the glass, and everything was dark,” creates atmosphere without beginning the action.

Revise so the environment participates in the choice:

> The emergency lamp reached only the two racks beside the door. Gao Huaiyin reached for a seedling tray, but its plastic rim clung to the iron shelf—the nutrient solution spilled that afternoon had frozen. Instead of pulling harder, she wrapped her scarf around the tray nearest the draft, then dragged the watering hose beneath the gap in the door. Water left inside had frozen into a row of rigid joints, preventing the door from closing.
>
> She followed the hose inward by touch and found the valve still dripping. If she saved the seedlings first, cold air would keep pouring in. If she went to shut the main valve, the trays by the door would remain where they were. She set the emergency lamp on the floor and told the neighbor who had just arrived, “You carry the trays. I’ll find the valve. Don’t pull—twist the ice loose from the rack first.”

The lamp’s reach, frozen nutrient solution, draft, and hose all change the task. The way Gao Huaiyin notices and handles them also shows that she knows the greenhouse. There is no need to add the scent of plants unless smell will indicate a leak or rot.

heading.zh: 环境描写显得水，怎样删改
heading.en: How to Cut or Revise Setting Description That Feels Like Padding

body.zh:
| 症状 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 开场先写一整段天气，再让人物出现 | 从人物受天气影响的第一个动作进入 |
| 罗列颜色、声音、气味，彼此无关 | 留下会影响判断或节奏的一两项 |
| 所有人都注意同样的景色 | 按人物目标与经验筛选细节 |
| 环境只负责象征人物心情 | 增加物理限制、信息或可用资源 |
| 场景条件写过后不再生效 | 让人物处理它，或删除这项条件 |
| 为了“不水”把地点删成空白 | 保留行动所需的距离、出口、障碍与可操作物 |

环境少写不等于不写。读者需要知道动作能否发生、危险从哪里来、人物能碰到什么。删的是不参与体验的清单，不是空间因果。
body.en:
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| An opening describes a full passage of weather before the character appears | Enter on the character’s first action affected by the weather |
| Colors, sounds, and smells are listed without connection | Keep the one or two details that alter judgment or rhythm |
| Everyone notices the same view | Filter details through each character’s goal and experience |
| The setting only symbolizes a character’s mood | Add a physical constraint, information, or usable resource |
| A condition never matters after it is described | Make the character handle it, or delete it |
| In avoiding padding, the writer strips the location into a blank | Preserve distances, exits, obstacles, and usable objects required for action |

Writing less setting does not mean writing none. Readers need to know whether an action is possible, where danger comes from, and what the character can reach. Remove the list that does not participate in experience, not the spatial cause and effect.

q.zh: 环境描写一定要推动剧情吗？
q.en: Must every setting description advance the plot?

a.zh: 不必每句都制造事件。它也可以建立气氛、节奏和人物体验；但应改变读者对现场的感受或理解。纯重复已知气氛、删掉无损的装饰可以压缩。
a.en: No. Description can also establish atmosphere, rhythm, and character experience, but it should change how readers feel or understand the scene. Decoration that merely repeats a known mood and can be removed without loss may be compressed.

q.zh: 五感是不是写得越多越有画面？
q.en: Does using more senses always make a scene more vivid?

a.zh: 不是。选择人物此刻最敏感、最能影响动作的感受即可。感官齐全却没有注意重点，反而会冲淡画面。
a.en: No. Choose the sensation the character is most sensitive to now and that most affects the action. Covering every sense without a focus can dilute the image instead.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 里说：“用 /story-long-write 修改这段环境描写，先确认人物当前目标，再保留会帮助、阻碍、误导或逼迫行动的细节，写出注意、交互和后果；不新增剧情条件，不为凑五感补描写”（Codex 中使用 `$story-long-write`）。
text.en: In Claude Code, say: “Use `/story-long-write` to revise this setting description. First identify the character’s current goal, then keep details that help, obstruct, mislead, or pressure the action. Show attention, interaction, and consequence. Add no new plot conditions, and do not add description merely to cover all five senses.” In Codex, use `$story-long-write`.

title.zh: 小说改短剧怎么删角色、合并角色：先保住人物功能
title.en: Short Drama: Preserve Character Function Before Cutting or Merging

seo_title.zh: 小说改短剧怎么删角色与合并角色｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Merge Characters for Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 短剧改编压缩人物，先删不保留的支线，再按行动、信息、关系与因果功能判断是否合并，并修复知情范围和铺垫。附原创展馆案例。
description.en: Cut subplots first, then merge characters by action, information, relationships, and causality. Includes a function ledger and an original gallery example.

answer.zh: 删角色前先列出他迫使谁选择、掌握什么信息、处在什么关系位置，以及为后文建立了哪条因果。先决定整条支线是否保留，再处理人物合并。只有两个角色的功能能由同一个目标、知情范围和关系位置自洽承担时才合并；转移出去的证据、许可、反对或牺牲要写明由谁接住。人物变少不是成功标准，因果不断、冲突不塌、观众不会提前知道答案才是。
answer.en: Before cutting a character, list whom they force to choose, what information they hold, where they stand in the relationship map, and which later cause and effect depends on them. Decide whether an entire subplot remains before merging characters. Merge only when one coherent goal, knowledge boundary, and relationship position can carry both characters’ functions. State who inherits any transferred evidence, permission, opposition, or sacrifice. Fewer characters is not the measure of success; causality must remain intact, conflict must survive, and the audience must not learn answers too early.

heading.zh: 先为候选角色做一张功能账
heading.en: Start with a Function Ledger for Every Candidate Character

body.zh:
| 角色 | 迫使谁作选择 | 独有信息或资源 | 关系位置 | 后续依赖 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 姓名或称呼 | 造成哪次决定 | 证据、权限、技能、误信 | 亲属、债主、同事、对手等 | 哪个揭示或结果需要他 |

“负责搞笑”“戏份不多”不足以决定去留。一个只出现两场的人，可能是主角取得许可证的唯一来源；一个出现很多次的人，也可能只重复别人已经完成的说明。先写功能，再讨论删、并或换载体。
body.en:
| Character | Whom do they force to choose? | Exclusive information or resource | Relationship position | Later dependency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name or role | Which decision do they cause? | Evidence, access, skill, or false belief | Relative, creditor, colleague, opponent, and so on | Which revelation or result requires them? |

“Provides comic relief” and “has few scenes” are not enough to decide whether someone stays. A person appearing in only two scenes may be the protagonist’s sole route to a permit. Someone with many appearances may merely repeat an explanation already delivered by others. Write the functions before discussing deletion, combination, or a different carrier.

heading.zh: 压缩顺序：先删线，再合并人物
heading.en: Compression Order: Cut Plotlines Before Merging Characters

body.zh:
先问某条支线是否仍属于这版短剧的核心承诺。若整条线删除，就把它的铺垫、兑现和孤儿线索一起处理，并逐项决定其中功能是随线删除，还是转移给保留线。

之后才合并人物。否则刚把证据和关系搬到某人身上，又发现他的整条线不保留，会造成重复返工。删线也不能只看节奏快慢：有些慢场建立信任、取得手段或制造信息差，删掉后，后面的快场虽然还在，却失去成立条件。
body.en:
First ask whether a subplot still belongs to the core promise of this short-drama version. If you remove the entire line, handle its setup, payoff, and orphaned clues together. For each function within it, decide whether it disappears with the line or transfers to a retained one.

Only then merge characters. Otherwise, you may move evidence and relationships onto someone whose entire line is later removed, creating duplicate work. Do not cut a subplot merely because it is slower. Some slow scenes establish trust, secure a means, or create an information gap; remove them and the later fast scenes may remain while losing the conditions that make them work.

heading.zh: 合并前过五道检查
heading.en: Pass Five Checks Before a Merge

body.zh:
1. **目标**：同一个人能否同时想要这两件事，还是会自相矛盾？
2. **知情范围**：合并后是否会让秘密提前泄露，或让人物知道来源不明的事实？
3. **关系位置**：支持者与施压者若合成一人，原有对抗是否消失？
4. **行动条件**：同一人在时间和空间上能否完成两项关键行动？
5. **代价**：原本的背叛、证言、拒绝或牺牲，会不会因为合并而失去重量？

若只有部分功能能合并，不必强求“二合一”。可以合并日常事务，却把独有证据转给另一个已经保留、且有合理取得路径的角色。
body.en:
1. **Goal:** Can one person coherently want both things, or do the desires contradict each other?
2. **Knowledge boundary:** Does the merge reveal a secret early or give the character a fact with no source?
3. **Relationship position:** If supporter and pressure source become one person, does the original opposition disappear?
4. **Conditions for action:** Can one person perform both crucial actions within the story’s time and space?
5. **Cost:** Does the original betrayal, testimony, refusal, or sacrifice lose weight after the merge?

If only some functions combine, do not force a complete two-into-one merge. Routine tasks can be merged while exclusive evidence moves to another retained character who has a plausible way to obtain it.

heading.zh: 原创范例：闭馆前的社区展厅
heading.en: Original Example: A Community Gallery Before Closing

body.zh:
虚构小说写青年策展人顾葵抢救一批即将被清退的社区口述录音。原著里有四名配角：保安老任掌握夜间进馆权限；物业主管只负责白天开门；志愿者小禾整理录音并发现编号缺页；赞助人周总以续租为条件要求撤下一段工伤证言。另有一条老任寻找失散战友录音的支线。

改编版不保留寻找战友支线。先删线，意味着相关照片、查询和结尾团聚一起删除；但老任的夜间权限仍是主线手段，不能因支线删掉就凭空消失。

如果把老任与小禾直接合成“保安兼整理员”，会产生知情穿帮：这个人既早就掌握门禁，又从一开始接触全部录音，顾葵便无需冒险争取协助，缺页线索和进馆手段也会过早集中在一个人手里。

可用方案是保留小禾，把老任与一位原著中只负责开门的物业主管合并。合并后的物业主管仍不知道录音内容，只能决定闭馆后是否放顾葵进去；小禾保留编号知识与发现缺页的行动。为了让许可有代价，物业主管要求顾葵在天亮前恢复消防通道，否则将按规定封存全部展品。

这样人物减少了一名，但三项功能仍分开：权限、证据、压力。周总的撤展要求与消防时限在同一夜碰撞，短剧获得更集中场面，却没有让任何人提前知道不该知道的事实。
body.en:
In a fictional novel, young curator Gu Kui is trying to save a collection of community oral-history recordings that will soon be removed. The source novel has four supporting characters: security guard Old Ren controls nighttime access to the gallery; a property manager only opens the door during the day; volunteer Xiao He catalogs the recordings and discovers a missing numbered page; and sponsor Mr. Zhou demands the removal of testimony about a workplace injury as a condition of renewing the lease. A separate subplot follows Old Ren searching the recordings for a comrade he lost contact with.

The adaptation drops the search-for-the-comrade subplot. Cutting the line first means removing its photographs, searches, and final reunion together. Old Ren’s nighttime access, however, remains a means needed by the main plot and cannot simply vanish with the subplot.

Directly merging Old Ren and Xiao He into a “security guard who also catalogs recordings” breaks the knowledge boundaries. This person would control access and have handled every recording from the start. Gu Kui would no longer need to risk winning an ally, while the missing-page clue and the means of entry would concentrate in one person too early.

A workable approach keeps Xiao He and merges Old Ren with the property manager whose only role in the source was opening the door. The merged property manager still knows nothing about the recordings and can decide only whether to admit Gu Kui after closing. Xiao He retains the numbering knowledge and the action of discovering the missing page. To give the permission a cost, the property manager requires Gu Kui to clear the fire exit before dawn or all exhibits will be sealed under the rules.

The cast loses one character while three functions remain separate: access, evidence, and pressure. Mr. Zhou’s removal demand and the fire-safety deadline collide on the same night, concentrating the short drama without letting anyone know facts they should not yet possess.

heading.zh: 删并之后，逐项修复因果桥
heading.en: Repair Every Causal Bridge After Cuts and Merges

body.zh:
用一条链回读每项重要结果：原因事实 → 人物怎样知道 → 作出什么选择 → 对方怎样反制 → 产生什么可见后果。角色删除后，最容易断在“怎样知道”和“怎样获得”。不能用一句“她早有准备”跨过去。

| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 因为名字多就合并 | 先比较功能、目标和关系位置 |
| 证人并入反派后仍保留秘密 | 重分信息来源，避免人物自我隐瞒 |
| 删除慢支线，主角突然拿到证据 | 为证据建立新的取得行动与代价 |
| 合并支持者和反对者，冲突消失 | 保留不同立场，或让其他关系承担压力 |
| 所有功能都塞给主角 | 保留需要他人许可、反制或独立选择的部分 |
| 删掉人物却留下无人兑现的伏笔 | 同步删除或明确转移每条铺垫 |

最后把每项改动写成“原功能 → 新承载者或删除 → 保住什么 → 损失什么”。若损失触及核心关系、关键选择或结局含义，应回退合并，不要靠对白解释。
body.en:
Read each important result back through one chain: causal fact → how a character learns it → what choice they make → how the other side counters → what visible consequence follows. After a character is removed, the chain most often breaks at “how they learn it” or “how they obtain it.” “She was prepared all along” cannot bridge the gap.

| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| Merging characters because there are too many names | Compare functions, goals, and relationship positions first |
| A witness is merged into the antagonist, yet the secret remains | Reassign the information source so the character is not hiding a fact from themself |
| A slow subplot is removed and the protagonist suddenly has the evidence | Establish a new action and cost through which the evidence is obtained |
| A supporter and opponent merge, erasing conflict | Keep the positions separate or let another relationship carry the pressure |
| Every function is assigned to the protagonist | Retain functions requiring another person’s permission, countermove, or independent choice |
| A character is removed but their setup remains with no payoff | Delete or explicitly transfer every setup at the same time |

Finally, write every change as: “original function → new carrier or deletion → what is preserved → what is lost.” If the loss affects a core relationship, crucial choice, or the ending’s meaning, reverse the merge rather than explaining it through dialogue.

q.zh: 短剧角色是不是越少越好？
q.en: Should a short drama always have as few characters as possible?

a.zh: 不是。角色数量服从故事功能和制作条件。删到同一人既提供证据、又制造阻力、又承担所有反应，容易让关系扁平或信息穿帮。
a.en: No. Cast size serves story function and production conditions. If one person supplies the evidence, creates the obstacle, and carries every reaction, relationships may flatten and knowledge boundaries may break.

q.zh: 两个作用相似的配角一定能合并吗？
q.en: Can two supporting characters with similar functions always be merged?

a.zh: 还要检查目标、知情范围、关系历史、时空条件和代价。都负责提供线索，但一人是亲属、一人是竞争者，合并可能改变主角为何相信这条线索。
a.en: You must also check goals, knowledge boundaries, relationship history, time and place, and cost. Two characters may both provide clues, but if one is family and the other a rival, merging them can change why the protagonist believes the clue.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-develop（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-develop`）只做人物压缩方案：按实际原著列角色的行动、信息、关系与因果功能，先标出可删支线，再检查合并后的知情范围和代价，并输出原功能到新承载者的对应；暂不写剧本。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-develop` only to create a character-compression plan. From the actual source novel, list each character’s action, information, relationship, and causal functions. Mark removable subplots first, then check knowledge boundaries and costs after each merge, and map every original function to its new carrier. Do not write the script yet. In Codex, use `$short-drama-develop`.

title.zh: 短剧证据镜头怎么拍：让观众看清，也看见后果
title.en: How to Shoot Evidence Reveals: Make the Proof and Consequences Clear

seo_title.zh: 短剧证据镜头怎么拍｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Shoot Evidence Reveals in Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 文件、手机、伤痕或物件成为证据时，先确定观众必须读到哪项特征，再安排控制权、揭示、接收反应和行动后果。附原创药房案例。
description.en: Define the feature viewers must read, then stage control, reveal, reaction, and consequence. Includes a pharmacy example with two temperature logs.

answer.zh: 证据镜头先回答五件事：证据在哪里、谁控制它、观众在揭示前知道什么、真正证明结论的是文字、形状、状态还是人物与物件的关系，以及谁看见后会改变行动。镜头无需按固定数量排列，但要给关键特征足够的尺度和时间，并让取得证据、读懂证据与证据造成的后果各有承载。
answer.en: An evidence shot must answer five questions: Where is the evidence? Who controls it? What does the audience know before the reveal? Is the conclusion proved by text, shape, condition, or the relationship between a person and an object? Who changes course after seeing it? The shots need no fixed count, but the decisive feature needs enough scale and screen time, while obtaining the evidence, understanding it, and acting on it each need a clear carrier.

heading.zh: 先确定证据究竟证明什么
heading.en: First Define Exactly What the Evidence Proves

body.zh:
“拍一张文件特写”仍不够具体。先写出观众必须得到的最小事实：是日期早于事故、签名与本人笔迹不符、包装封口已断，还是手机在某时仍连接现场网络。

| 证据类型 | 必须看清的东西 |
|---|---|
| 精确文字 | 具体词句、日期、号码或名字 |
| 形状与状态 | 断角、划痕、封口、缺页、开合 |
| 对照差异 | 两个版本之间唯一关键变化 |
| 关系证据 | 谁持有、谁能接触、物件出现在何处 |

一项证据通常只能支持有限判断。看见断封只能证明封口被动过，无法单独确定操作者或动机。
body.en:
“Shoot a close-up of the document” is still too vague. State the minimum fact the audience must learn: Is the date earlier than the accident? Does the signature differ from the person’s handwriting? Is the package seal broken? Was the phone still connected to the network at the location at a certain time?

| Evidence type | What must be legible |
|---|---|
| Exact text | A specific phrase, date, number, or name |
| Shape and condition | A broken corner, scratch, seal, missing page, or open/closed state |
| Comparative difference | The single decisive change between two versions |
| Relational evidence | Who holds it, who had access, or where the object appears |

One piece of evidence usually supports only a limited inference. A broken seal proves that the seal was disturbed; it cannot identify the person responsible or their motive by itself.

heading.zh: 把揭示拆成信息变化，而非镜头配额
heading.en: Break the Reveal into Changes in Information, Not a Shot Quota

body.zh:
证据场面可能包含方位、取得、展示、理解、反应和后果，但不要求六个镜头。先按信息变化组织：

- 建立证据与人物的空间关系；
- 某人取得、打开或让它进入可见状态；
- 观众读到关键特征；
- 接收者的判断发生变化；
- 新判断改变持物、站位、对白或下一动作。

两项变化能在同一双人镜里读清，就不必硬切。只有注意、解释、控制权或关系真的变化时再切镜。
body.en:
An evidence scene may involve position, acquisition, display, understanding, reaction, and consequence, but it does not require six shots. Organize it by changes in information:

- Establish the spatial relationship between the evidence and the characters.
- Let someone obtain it, open it, or make it visible.
- Let the audience read the decisive feature.
- Change the recipient’s judgment.
- Let the new judgment alter possession, position, dialogue, or the next action.

If two changes read clearly in one two-shot, do not cut merely to fill a pattern. Cut when attention, interpretation, control, or a relationship actually changes.

heading.zh: 文字证据与物件证据的可读方式不同
heading.en: Textual Evidence and Physical Evidence Need Different Readability

body.zh:
精确文字是证据时，先确认文字有准确版本，再选择直接呈现或后期排字；镜头要让承载面正对、无遮挡，并给观众读完的时间。一闪而过的手机屏不能只靠台词宣称“大家都看清了”。

若证据是纹样、裂口或物件位置，画面应强调这一特征，不要临时生成无关文字。证据被拿起、翻面或递交时，还要保持上一镜的持有人、方向和状态，避免关键特征在切镜后换边或消失。
body.en:
When exact wording is evidence, first establish an accurate text version, then choose whether to show it directly or typeset it in post. The surface should face the camera without obstruction, and viewers need enough time to read it. A phone screen that flashes past cannot become legible merely because a line of dialogue says that everyone saw it.

When the evidence is a pattern, crack, or object position, emphasize that feature instead of generating unrelated text. If someone picks up, turns over, or hands off the evidence, preserve the holder, orientation, and condition from the previous shot so the decisive feature does not switch sides or disappear after the cut.

heading.zh: 原创范例：药房冰柜里的两张温度签
heading.en: Original Example: Two Temperature Logs in a Pharmacy Refrigerator

body.zh:
社区药房停电后，一批需要低温保存的药品被判定报废。店长拿出一张手写温度签，称停电只持续了十分钟；夜班药师夏禾发现冰柜背面还贴着自动记录纸。

**镜头一，中景双人**：店长站在冰柜与夏禾之间，把手写签举在胸前。职责是建立谁控制证据、谁被挡在外面。

**镜头二，跟随动作的近景**：夏禾不去抢手写签，而是拉开冰柜侧面的检修板；一条记录纸被卡在滚轴上。职责是取得第二项证据，记录纸尚未读清。

**镜头三，记录纸与手写签同框**：纸上的停电区间跨过数小时，手写签只覆盖最后十分钟。若精确时间由后期排字，此镜预留清楚纸面并完成最终合成。职责是让观众完成对照。

**镜头四，双人中景**：排队等药的人停止递处方，店长把手写签降到桌下；夏禾把记录纸留在柜门上，拨打批次冻结电话。职责是让证据改变公开信任和下一行动。

单拍记录纸不足以证明店长故意造假，因此夏禾冻结批次、要求调查，没有直接宣布犯罪动机。
body.en:
After a power outage at a community pharmacy, a batch of temperature-sensitive medicine is marked for disposal. The manager produces a handwritten temperature tag and claims the outage lasted only ten minutes. Night pharmacist Xia He notices a strip of automatic recorder paper still attached behind the refrigerator.

**Shot one, medium two-shot:** The manager stands between Xia He and the refrigerator, holding the handwritten tag at chest level. Its job is to establish who controls the evidence and who is being kept away.

**Shot two, close shot following the action:** Instead of grabbing the tag, Xia He opens the refrigerator’s side service panel. A strip of recorder paper is caught in the roller. Its job is to obtain a second piece of evidence; the record is not yet readable.

**Shot three, recorder paper and handwritten tag in the same frame:** The outage interval on the paper spans several hours, while the handwritten tag covers only the final ten minutes. If the exact times will be typeset in post, this shot reserves a clear view of the paper for final compositing. Its job is to let the audience compare the records.

**Shot four, medium two-shot:** People waiting for medicine stop handing over their prescriptions. The manager lowers the handwritten tag beneath the table. Xia He leaves the recorder paper on the refrigerator door and calls to place the batch on hold. Its job is to change public trust and the next action.

The recorder paper alone does not prove that the manager deliberately falsified anything. Xia He therefore places the batch on hold and requests an investigation rather than declaring a criminal motive.

heading.zh: 证据镜头常见失效
heading.en: Common Ways Evidence Shots Fail

body.zh:
| 失效 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 只有文件特写，不知道它证明什么 | 写出最小事实与结论边界 |
| 观众还没读完就切走 | 调整尺度、遮挡和停留，或拆出可读镜头 |
| 人物念完全文代替画面 | 只说争议点，让画面承担可见依据 |
| 揭示后所有人轮流震惊 | 选会改变风险的代表反应或群体状态 |
| 证据切镜后换手、翻面或变版本 | 对齐上一镜终点与下一镜起点 |
| 证据出现后行动没有变化 | 让判断落到拒绝、追问、封存、交出或离场 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| A document gets a close-up, but no one knows what it proves | State the minimum fact and the boundary of the inference |
| The shot cuts before viewers finish reading | Adjust scale, obstruction, and duration, or separate a readable shot |
| A character reads the entire document aloud instead of letting the image work | Speak only the disputed point and let the visible evidence support it |
| Everyone takes turns looking shocked after the reveal | Choose the representative reaction or group-state change that alters risk |
| After a cut, the evidence changes hands, flips, or becomes another version | Match the ending state of one shot to the starting state of the next |
| Nothing changes after the evidence appears | Turn the judgment into a refusal, question, hold, surrender, or departure |

q.zh: 证据一定要给特写吗？
q.en: Does evidence always need a close-up?

a.zh: 不需要。若证据在谁手里、谁拒绝接触更重要，中景或双人镜更清楚；只有关键特征太小、必须单独读取时才收近。
a.en: No. If who holds the evidence or who refuses to touch it matters more, a medium shot or two-shot may be clearer. Move closer only when the decisive feature is too small and must be read on its own.

q.zh: 手机聊天记录应该全部拍出来吗？
q.en: Should a phone chat be shown in full?

a.zh: 只呈现当前结论必需的消息、时间或发送者，并保证文字版本准确。无关长对话会延长阅读并增加制作负担。
a.en: Show only the message, time, or sender required for the present conclusion, and make sure the text version is accurate. Irrelevant long exchanges increase reading time and production work.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-storyboard（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-storyboard`）只设计这个证据揭示：写清证据控制者、观众必须读到的最小事实、呈现尺度、谁先看见、接收反应和后续行动；不改证据内容，不扩到全片分镜。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-storyboard` only to design this evidence reveal. Specify who controls the evidence, the minimum fact viewers must read, presentation scale, who sees it first, the recipient’s reaction, and the resulting action. Do not change the evidence or expand into a full-film storyboard. In Codex, use `$short-drama-storyboard`.

title.zh: AI短剧道具参考图怎么做：把形制、状态和文字分开
title.en: AI Short-Drama Prop Boards: Separate Form, State & Text

seo_title.zh: AI短剧道具参考图怎么做｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: AI Short-Drama Prop Reference Images | ZenStory

description.zh: 可复用道具参考图先固定尺度、轮廓、材质和功能件，再单列当前开合、损伤、内容物与文字方式。附原创录音机参考板。
description.en: Fix a prop’s scale, form, materials, and working parts; list current open/closed state, damage, contents, and text separately. Includes a recorder board.

answer.zh: AI短剧道具参考图要先固定不会随一场动作轻易改变的身份：尺度、主要比例、轮廓、材料、接缝、开口与功能件；再单列当前状态，例如开合、损伤、污渍、内容物和文字版本。选择足以识别结构的正侧视或局部视图，并为可读文字、图形符号、空白承载面或后期排字选一种处理。参考图只展示已确定状态，不提前演完剧情动作。
answer.en: For an AI short-drama prop reference, first fix the identity that should not change casually with one scene’s action: scale, major proportions, silhouette, materials, seams, openings, and functional parts. Then specify the current state, such as open or closed, damage, stains, contents, and text version. Choose front, side, or detail views that make the structure recognizable. For text, choose one treatment: accurately readable wording, graphic marks, a blank surface, or later typesetting. A reference image shows an established state; it should not perform the entire story action in advance.

heading.zh: 先分清道具身份与当前状态
heading.en: Separate the Prop’s Lasting Identity from Its Current State

body.zh:
| 层次 | 参考图要固定什么 | 示例 |
|---|---|---|
| 持久身份 | 尺度、轮廓、比例、材料、功能结构、永久磨损 | 铰链方向、把手形状、固定缺口 |
| 当前状态 | 开合、损伤、污渍、内容物、持有关系、文字版本 | 盖子打开、磁带在内、标签已撕半 |

换手、打开或沾水通常只是状态变化，不应重新设计成另一件道具。真正改变形制和功能的不可逆改造，才需要另行决定是否建立新版身份。
body.en:
| Layer | What the reference must fix | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Lasting identity | Scale, silhouette, proportions, materials, functional structure, and permanent wear | Hinge direction, handle shape, fixed notch |
| Current state | Open or closed, damage, stains, contents, who holds it, and text version | Lid open, cassette inside, label half torn away |

Changing hands, opening, or getting wet is usually a state change and should not redesign the item into a different prop. Only an irreversible modification that truly changes its form and function calls for deciding whether to establish a new identity version.

heading.zh: 一张可复用道具板写哪些信息
heading.en: What to Include on a Reusable Prop Board

body.zh:
按使用目的选择必要项：

1. 道具类型与剧情用途；
2. 真实尺度或中性参照，以及长宽厚比例；
3. 主材、次材、反光、透明或粗糙关系；
4. 接缝、扣件、开口、握持面和活动方向；
5. 当前损伤、内容物与表面状态；
6. 正面、侧面、背面或关键局部中真正有用的视图；
7. 文字承载面怎样处理；
8. 需要保持与排除的变形、错材、错状态和多余复制品。

尺度参照优先使用无身份的常见物或明确尺寸关系，避免让某个剧情人物的手成为默认参考，从而把人物也粘进道具资产。
body.en:
Choose only what the intended use requires:

1. Prop type and story function.
2. Real scale or a neutral reference, plus length-width-thickness proportions.
3. Primary and secondary materials, including reflective, transparent, and rough relationships.
4. Seams, fasteners, openings, grip surfaces, and directions of movement.
5. Current damage, contents, and surface state.
6. Only the useful front, side, back, or key detail views.
7. The treatment for any text-bearing surface.
8. Deformations, wrong materials, wrong states, and extra duplicate props that must be excluded.

Prefer an identity-neutral common object or an explicit size relationship as the scale reference. Avoid using a story character’s hand by default, which can bind that character into the prop asset as well.

heading.zh: 道具上的字先选处理方式
heading.en: Choose How to Handle Text on the Prop First

body.zh:
- **准确可读**：剧情要求观众逐字读懂，保存确定文本及承载位置。
- **图形存在**：只需看到标签或刻痕的布局，不产生可辨的新名字和号码。
- **保持空白**：本轮画面不应出现字，同时保留承载面的材质与透视。
- **后期添加**：先留无遮挡、可跟踪透视的干净区域，准确文字在后期完成。

这些方式不能同时套在同一承载面。选择后期排字，不等于最终镜头可以忘记补字；选择准确可读，也不能再全局要求“不要任何文字”。
body.en:
- **Accurately readable:** The plot requires viewers to read the wording exactly, so preserve the approved text and its location.
- **Graphic presence:** The label or engraving layout must be visible, without generating a legible new name or number.
- **Keep blank:** No text should appear in this image, while the material and perspective of the text-bearing surface remain.
- **Add in post:** Leave a clean, unobstructed area with trackable perspective, then add exact text during post-production.

These treatments cannot all apply to the same surface. Choosing later typesetting does not mean the final shot may forget to add the text. Choosing accurately readable wording cannot coexist with a global instruction to remove all text.

heading.zh: 原创范例：档案采访用的便携录音机
heading.en: Original Example: A Portable Recorder for Archive Interviews

body.zh:
故事中的旧录音机保存了一段被覆盖过的采访。可复用参考板先固定身份：巴掌宽的扁长机身，深绿色磨砂塑料；左侧一枚银色滑杆，正面双圆轴窗，底部电池盖有斜向裂缝，右上角网罩凹陷。比例、裂缝与滑杆位置是跨镜识别点。

当前状态 A 是“合盖、空仓、滑杆停在停止位”；状态 B 是“仓盖打开，透明磁带在内，左卷带量较少”。两种状态分开呈现，不在一张图里同时要求仓盖开与关。

磁带标签上的采访编号必须在后续镜头读清，因此本次参考板为标签预留正对视线的浅色区域，准确编号交给后期；机身原有的模糊品牌位只保留几何凹槽，不临时编造文字。

建议视图包括：正面全貌固定轮廓与轴窗；侧面固定滑杆和厚度；开仓局部固定铰链、磁带方向与电池盖裂缝。参考板不画角色按下播放键，也不提前出现转动结果；那属于具体镜头动作。
body.en:
An old recorder in the story preserves an interview that was partly overwritten. The reusable reference board first fixes its identity: a flat, elongated body about a palm wide, made of dark-green matte plastic; a silver slider on the left; two circular reel windows on the front; a diagonal crack across the battery cover below; and a dented grille at the upper right. Its proportions, crack, and slider location are recognition anchors across shots.

Current state A is “compartment closed, empty, slider in the stop position.” State B is “compartment open, clear cassette inside, less tape on the left reel.” Show the states separately rather than asking one image to display the compartment both open and closed.

The interview number on the cassette label must be readable in a later shot. This reference board therefore reserves a light-colored label area facing the viewer and leaves the exact number for post-production. The recorder’s blurred brand area retains only its geometric groove; no temporary wording is invented.

Useful views include a front overview fixing the silhouette and reel windows, a side view fixing the slider and thickness, and an open-compartment detail fixing the hinge, cassette orientation, and battery-cover crack. The reference board does not show a character pressing Play or reveal the reels turning ahead of time. Those belong to a specific shot action.

heading.zh: 道具参考图常见失败
heading.en: Common Prop Reference Failures

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 只写“古老、精致、神秘” | 补尺度、轮廓、材料和功能结构 |
| 开、关、完好、破损同时出现 | 每张状态图只选一个明确时点 |
| 不同视图里缺口和活动件换位 | 先固定身份锚点与视图方向 |
| 用角色手作比例，人物也被复制 | 改用中性参照或明确尺寸关系 |
| 临时编造标签文字 | 选择准确文本、图形、空白或后期方式 |
| 为展示功能直接演完剧情动作 | 参考板展示结构和起始状态，动作留给镜头 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| The prompt says only “old, exquisite, mysterious” | Add scale, silhouette, materials, and functional structure |
| Open, closed, intact, and damaged states appear together | Choose one clear moment for each state image |
| Notches and moving parts shift between views | Fix identity anchors and viewing directions first |
| A character’s hand sets scale, so the person is duplicated too | Use a neutral reference or explicit size relationship |
| The system invents temporary label text | Choose exact text, graphics, blank space, or post-production |
| The board performs the plot action to demonstrate function | Show structure and starting state; leave action to the shot |

q.zh: 一个道具需要画几个视图？
q.en: How many views does one prop need?

a.zh: 看识别与使用需要。正面足以固定轮廓时无需凑视图；背部机关、开启方向或关键损伤不可见时，再加侧面、背面或局部。
a.en: Use only the views required for recognition and use. If the front fixes the silhouette, do not add views to meet a quota. Add a side, back, or detail only when a rear mechanism, opening direction, or crucial damage is otherwise invisible.

q.zh: 道具坏了以后要重新做参考图吗？
q.en: Do I need a new reference image after the prop is damaged?

a.zh: 身份不变、损伤需要跨镜保持时，新增损坏状态参考即可。若损伤彻底改变形制或功能，再决定是否建立新版身份。
a.en: If its identity remains the same and the damage must persist across shots, add a damaged-state reference. If the damage fundamentally changes form or function, then decide whether to create a new identity version.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-image-prompts（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-image-prompts`）为这个已确定道具整理参考图提示词：分开持久身份与当前状态，写尺度、轮廓、材料、功能件、必要视图和文字处理；只做参考板，不生成剧情动作。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-image-prompts` to prepare reference-image prompts for this established prop. Separate lasting identity from current state, and specify scale, silhouette, materials, functional parts, necessary views, and text treatment. Create only the reference-board prompt, not a story action. In Codex, use `$short-drama-image-prompts`.

title.zh: 短剧内心戏怎么写：把心理活动变成可表演信息
title.en: How to Write Inner Monologue for Short Drama: Make It Performable

seo_title.zh: 短剧内心戏怎么写｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: How to Write Inner Monologue for Short Drama | ZenStory

description.zh: 小说心理描写改成短剧时，先保留它改变选择的作用，再在行动、证据、空间、对白与有意旁白中选载体。附原创冷库案例。
description.en: Preserve how a thought changes a choice, then carry it through action, evidence, space, dialogue, or deliberate voice-over. Includes a cold-room example.

answer.zh: 把小说心理活动改成短剧，先写清这层内心使人物怎样判断、选择或隐瞒，再选择观众能接收的载体。优先让行动后果、证据反应、空间位置或关系动作承担意义；确实需要把私人想法直接交给观众时，再有意使用内心声音。无论选择哪种方式，都要分清观众听见了什么、现场其他人物是否听见，以及这条信息怎样改变下一步。
answer.en: When adapting internal narration from a novel into short drama, first state how the thought changes what the character judges, chooses, or conceals. Then choose a carrier the audience can receive. Prefer consequences of action, responses to evidence, spatial position, or relational action. Use an inner voice deliberately when a private thought must reach the audience directly. Whichever method you choose, distinguish what the audience hears from what other characters hear, and show how the information changes the next step.

heading.zh: 先保住内心描写的作用，再换载体
heading.en: Preserve the Function of the Thought Before Changing Its Form

body.zh:
把原文中的心理句改写成一句功能说明：人物因此相信什么、害怕失去什么、准备隐瞒什么，或决定怎样做。保留作用，不必保留原句形状。

| 原文作用 | 可用屏幕载体 |
|---|---|
| 判断对方在撒谎 | 核对证据、改变问法、暂不揭穿 |
| 想离开又舍不得 | 走到出口又把关键物件留下 |
| 不愿承认失败 | 拒绝帮助、改口谈条件、藏起结果 |
| 私人记忆影响选择 | 触发物与当下行动，或明确的主观声音 |

若一句心理话删掉后人物行为完全不变，它可能只是解释。若行为会变，就必须让这个变化被演出来或被有意听见。
body.en:
Rewrite each internal sentence from the source as a functional statement: What does the character now believe, fear losing, plan to conceal, or decide to do? Preserve that function rather than the sentence’s original shape.

| Function in the source | Possible screen carrier |
|---|---|
| Judges that someone is lying | Checks evidence, changes the question, or delays confrontation |
| Wants to leave but cannot let go | Reaches the exit but leaves a crucial object behind |
| Refuses to admit failure | Rejects help, renegotiates, or hides the result |
| A private memory changes a choice | A trigger and present action, or a clearly marked subjective voice |

If deleting a thought leaves the character’s behavior completely unchanged, it may only be explanation. If the behavior changes, that change must either be performed or deliberately heard.

heading.zh: 五种载体怎么选
heading.en: How to Choose Among Five Carriers

body.zh:
1. **行动后果**：人物做或不做一件有结果的事。
2. **证据反应**：他验证、藏起、退回或重新排列某项证据。
3. **空间动作**：靠近谁、挡住出口、换到另一方身边。
4. **关系对白**：把想法变成试探、拒绝、交换或质问，现场人物也会听见。
5. **主观声音**：只把必须明确而又不适合说出口的信息交给观众。

不要为每句心理活动配一个无功能微动作。倒水、看窗或攥手若没有改变议程与证据，只是把解释换成假运动。
body.en:
1. **Consequence of action:** The character does or declines something that produces a result.
2. **Response to evidence:** They verify, hide, return, or rearrange a piece of evidence.
3. **Spatial action:** They approach someone, block an exit, or move to the other person’s side.
4. **Relational dialogue:** The thought becomes a probe, refusal, exchange, or challenge that people in the scene can also hear.
5. **Subjective voice:** Give the audience only the private information that must be explicit but cannot naturally be spoken.

Do not assign a purposeless micro-gesture to every thought. Pouring water, looking out a window, or clenching a fist merely turns explanation into fake movement unless it changes the agenda, evidence, or choice.

heading.zh: 旁白、对白与留白会改变谁知道什么
heading.en: Voice-Over, Dialogue, and Silence Change Who Knows What

body.zh:
同一句“我不信他忘了密码”，写成对白，听者会知道自己被怀疑；写成明确的内心声音，观众知道，现场人物不知道；完全不说，则需要可见证据让观众推断。三种选择会打开不同后续。

选择声音时写清声源和时空关系。电话里的现场声音、人物没有入画却在门外说话、事后叙述和人物内心，属于不同通道。下场戏只能继承人物实际听见或看见的信息，不能因为观众听过旁白，就让对手自动知情。
body.en:
Take the same thought: “I don’t believe he forgot the password.” Spoken as dialogue, the listener knows they are suspected. Presented as a clearly marked inner voice, the audience knows but people in the scene do not. Left unspoken, it requires visible evidence from which the audience can infer it. Each option opens a different next scene.

When using voice, state its source and relationship to time and space. Live sound over a phone, a character speaking outside the door while offscreen, retrospective narration, and private thought are different channels. The next scene can inherit only what a character actually heard or saw. An opponent does not automatically know something merely because the audience heard it in voice-over.

heading.zh: 原创范例：冷库门上的第二层霜
heading.en: Original Example: A Second Layer of Frost on a Cold-Storage Door

body.zh:
食品检测员唐郁陪仓库主管检查一批被退货的冷冻浆果。小说原句是：“她忽然明白，主管早就进过这间封存冷库，只是在等她替他签字。”

可表演版本不直接解释：

> 主管把封存表推到她面前。唐郁没有接笔。她蹲下看门锁，锁孔周围结着新霜，霜下却压着半枚已经断开的红色封签。
>
> 唐郁把自己的空白封签放在旁边，没有贴。
>
> 唐郁：你先写开门时间。
>
> 主管：现在补也一样。
>
> 唐郁把表转回去，压在他的钥匙串下。
>
> 唐郁：那就由开门的人签。

断签让她形成判断；不接笔、要求时间、把表退回去让判断改变行动。主管能听见质问，却不知道她是否还发现了别的痕迹。若作品需要观众准确知道她的怀疑，可以在看见断签后加一句内心声音；加了以后仍保留退表动作，因为意义需要产生后果。
body.en:
Food inspector Tang Yu accompanies a warehouse supervisor to inspect returned frozen berries. The source novel says, “She suddenly understood that the supervisor had already entered the sealed cold room and was merely waiting for her to sign on his behalf.”

A performable version does not explain it directly:

> The supervisor pushes the seal form toward her. Tang Yu does not take the pen. She crouches to inspect the lock. Fresh frost surrounds the keyhole, but beneath it lies half of a red security seal that has already been broken.
>
> Tang Yu places her blank seal beside it without attaching it.
>
> Tang Yu: Write down the time you opened the door first.
>
> Supervisor: Filling it in now makes no difference.
>
> Tang Yu turns the form back and pins it beneath his key ring.
>
> Tang Yu: Then the person who opened it should sign.

The broken seal produces her judgment. Refusing the pen, demanding the time, and returning the form turn that judgment into action. The supervisor hears the accusation but does not know whether she has found any other trace. If the work requires the audience to know her suspicion precisely, add one line of inner voice after she sees the seal. Keep the action of returning the form, because the meaning still needs a consequence.

heading.zh: 内心戏常见失败与修正
heading.en: Common Inner-Monologue Failures and Fixes

body.zh:
| 失败 | 修正 |
|---|---|
| 动作段写“他意识到、她觉得” | 找到该认识改变的下一动作 |
| 每层心理都改成旁白 | 只保留必须直接给观众的私人信息 |
| 用攥拳、皱眉替代所有想法 | 让动作作用于证据、关系或选择 |
| 私人旁白说完，对手立刻接话 | 分清现场人物与观众的知情范围 |
| 完全留白，观众没有推断依据 | 提供一个能支持判断的行为或证据 |
| 旁白与画面重复同一事实 | 让声音增加画面无法独立给出的层次，或删掉 |
body.en:
| Failure | Fix |
|---|---|
| An action paragraph says “he realized” or “she felt” | Find the next action changed by that realization |
| Every layer of thought becomes voice-over | Keep only private information that must reach the audience directly |
| Clenched fists and frowns stand in for every thought | Make the action affect evidence, a relationship, or a choice |
| An opponent answers immediately after private voice-over | Separate what characters in the scene know from what the audience knows |
| Everything is left implicit, with no basis for inference | Supply one behavior or piece of evidence that supports the judgment |
| Voice-over repeats exactly what the image already shows | Let sound add a layer the image cannot provide, or remove it |

q.zh: 内心旁白是不是越少越好？
q.en: Should inner voice-over always be kept to a minimum?

a.zh: 没有统一多少。先看作品是否选择主观声音，以及信息能否由更有后果的行动承担。旁白能明确私人判断，但也会改变观众知情位置。
a.en: There is no universal amount. First consider whether the work uses a subjective voice and whether the information can be carried by an action with greater consequences. Voice-over can clarify private judgment, but it also changes the audience’s knowledge position.

q.zh: 人物沉默能表现心理吗？
q.en: Can silence express a character’s thoughts?

a.zh: 可以，前提是沉默有对象并改变现场，例如拒绝回答使对方换策略。没有压力与后果的停顿只会留下空白。
a.en: Yes, if the silence has an object and changes the scene—for example, refusing to answer makes the other person change tactics. A pause without pressure or consequence only leaves a blank.

text.zh: 在 Claude Code 中用 /short-drama-write（Codex 中用 `$short-drama-write`）检查这段内心戏：先列心理信息改变的判断与选择，再比较行动、证据、空间、对白和主观声音载体；标清观众与现场人物分别知道什么，只改这一场，不扩写分镜。
text.en: In Claude Code, use `/short-drama-write` to inspect this inner-monologue passage. First list the judgments and choices changed by the psychological information, then compare action, evidence, space, dialogue, and subjective voice as carriers. Mark separately what the audience and the people in the scene know. Revise only this scene, without expanding it into a storyboard. In Codex, use `$short-drama-write`.

title.zh: 小说改短剧怎么调整时间线：重排顺序，别打断因果
title.en: Reordering a Novel Timeline for Short Drama Without Breaking Causality

seo_title.zh: 改编怎么调整剧情时间线｜ZenStory
seo_title.en: Reordering a Story Timeline for Adaptation | ZenStory

description.zh: 小说改短剧重排剧情时，先画出知识、道具、关系、铺垫与后果的依赖，再选择观众何时知道什么。附原创山地救援案例。
description.en: Map knowledge, prop, relationship, setup, and consequence dependencies before choosing when viewers learn each fact. Includes a mountain-rescue example.

answer.zh: 改编重排时间线前，先把每个关键事件依赖的知识、道具、关系、伤势与公开范围写清。移动一场戏后，检查人物是否提前使用尚未获得的信息或物件、关系结果是否跑到原因之前、铺垫是否晚于兑现。随后重新选择观众的信息位置：先知道真相制造悬念，和人物一起知道制造惊讶。倒叙、并行和跳时都可以使用，但进入、退出与返回当前线的边界要清楚，重排必须保住人物选择成立的因果桥。
answer.en: Before reordering an adaptation timeline, record the knowledge, props, relationships, injuries, and public or private status on which each crucial event depends. After moving a scene, check that no character uses information or an object before obtaining it, no relationship outcome precedes its cause, and no setup arrives after its payoff. Then choose the audience’s information position: knowing the truth first creates suspense; learning it with the character creates surprise. Flashbacks, parallel lines, and time jumps all work when their entrances, exits, and return to the current line are clear. Reordering must preserve the causal bridge that makes each choice credible.

heading.zh: 先说明为什么要重排
heading.en: First State Why You Want to Reorder the Timeline

body.zh:
重排可以让开场更快进入压力、把相邻的重复说明合并，或改变观众获得真相的时机。它不能只为了“更刺激”把结果搬到前面，却让人物的选择失去理由。

为每个拟移动片段写两句：原位置承担什么功能；新位置希望改变什么观看体验。说不出第二句，可能无需移动；说不出第一句，说明还没看清会丢掉什么。
body.en:
Reordering can bring pressure into the opening sooner, combine neighboring repeated explanations, or change when the audience learns the truth. It cannot move a result forward merely to feel “more exciting” while stripping the character’s choice of its reason.

For every passage you may move, write two sentences: What function does its original position serve? What viewing experience should the new position change? If you cannot answer the second, it may not need to move. If you cannot answer the first, you do not yet know what might be lost.

heading.zh: 画出五类不能倒置的依赖
heading.en: Map Five Dependencies That Cannot Be Reversed Carelessly

body.zh:
| 依赖 | 重排后要问 |
|---|---|
| 知识 | 人物何时亲眼看见、听见或被告知？ |
| 道具与权限 | 使用前是否已经取得，转手过程是否存在？ |
| 关系 | 信任、决裂或结盟是否先有触发与行动？ |
| 铺垫与兑现 | 观众是否在结果前拥有足够依据？ |
| 身体与公开状态 | 伤势、位置、时间，以及秘密公开给谁是否连续？ |

这些依赖不是要求一律顺叙。可以先展示后果，再回到原因；但后果段中的人物只能使用那个时点已经拥有的东西，观众也要清楚这是结果预览而非当前线继续。
body.en:
| Dependency | Question after reordering |
|---|---|
| Knowledge | When does the character see, hear, or learn it? |
| Props and authority | Was it obtained before use, and does the handoff exist? |
| Relationship | Does trust, rupture, or alliance have a prior trigger and action? |
| Setup and payoff | Does the audience have enough basis before the result? |
| Physical and public state | Are injury, location, time, and who knows a secret continuous? |

These dependencies do not require a chronological narrative. You may show a consequence and then return to its cause. In the consequence passage, however, characters can use only what they possessed at that moment, and the audience must understand that this is a preview of a result rather than continuation of the current line.

heading.zh: 重排同时是在选择观众知道什么
heading.en: Reordering Also Chooses What the Audience Knows

body.zh:
同一秘密有两种基本观看位置：观众先知道，重点变成角色何时发现、错误选择会造成什么；观众与角色同时知道，重点落在揭示本身。两种都成立，不能在镜头中偷偷给出真相，又让后续仍按观众完全不知来设计。

倒叙或并行段落进入时，用时间、地点、造型、声音或明确标记建立边界；退出后让当前线的问题继续运动。过去段只带回会改变当前理解的部分，避免为了补全资料暂停整集。
body.en:
One secret offers two basic audience positions. If the audience knows first, the focus becomes when the character will discover it and what their mistaken choices will cause. If the audience learns with the character, the reveal itself carries the emphasis. Both work. Do not quietly show the truth in a shot and then design later scenes as if viewers know nothing.

When entering a flashback or parallel passage, establish the boundary through time, location, appearance, sound, or an explicit marker. On exit, keep the current-line problem moving. A past passage should retrieve only what changes present understanding rather than pausing an entire episode to complete a dossier.

heading.zh: 原创范例：被剪断的救援绳
heading.en: Original Example: The Cut Rescue Rope

body.zh:
原小说按顺序写：护林员周放借出一条橙色救援绳；搭档梁真私自剪下一段修补吊桥，把绑扎后多余的一小截收进工具包，绑在桥上的部分没有拆走；暴雨夜绳子长度不足，周放只能绕远路营救被困测绘员。改编想从暴雨夜开场，再逐步揭示绳子为什么变短。

**开场结果**：周放把绳头抛向对岸，绳子差半米。他发现断口是平整刀口，没有立刻知道谁剪过。此时他只能改变路线，不能提前质问梁真。

**当前线推进**：绕行途中，梁真从工具包拿出修桥剩下的同色短绳，捆紧担架上松动的工具包。观众得到“她接触过绳”的新依据，周放也在此刻看见，关系压力才进入现场。

**短回插**：由短绳上的桥木纤维触发，回到白天梁真剪绳、绑紧桥板后，把贴着木板量过的余料收进工具包的动作；片段同时交代她当时为了让村民过桥，却没有登记长度变化。

**返回与后果**：周放没有停下救援长篇争吵，而是把路线图交给梁真，让她带担架走自己修过的桥，并要求她承担桥况判断。过去信息改变当前分工；救援结束后，两人再处理隐瞒与责任。

如果开场直接拍清梁真剪绳，观众会先知道真相，体验偏向等待周放发现；若只拍刀口，观众和周放一起推断。二选一后，后续镜头都要继承对应知情位置。
body.en:
In the source novel, events occur in this order: forest ranger Zhou Fang lends out an orange rescue rope. His partner Liang Zhen secretly cuts off a length to repair a suspension bridge, puts the small excess piece left after tying it into her tool bag, and leaves the portion tied to the bridge in place. On a stormy night, the shortened rope cannot reach, so Zhou Fang must take a longer route to rescue a trapped surveyor. The adaptation wants to open on the storm and reveal gradually why the rope is short.

**Opening consequence:** Zhou Fang throws the rope end toward the opposite bank and comes up half a meter short. He sees that the cut is clean but does not yet know who cut it. At this point he can only change routes; he cannot confront Liang Zhen in advance.

**Current line advances:** During the detour, Liang Zhen takes the matching short piece from her tool bag and secures loose equipment on the stretcher. The audience receives new evidence that she handled the rope, and Zhou Fang sees it at this moment, so pressure enters their relationship only now.

**Brief insert:** Fibers from the bridge timber on the short rope trigger a return to daytime. Liang Zhen cuts the rope, secures the bridge plank, and places the excess she measured against the timber into her tool bag. The passage also establishes that she acted to let villagers cross and failed to record the changed length.
